sentences.zh: 阿離合懣

translations.literal: Ali Hemen
translations.idiomatic: Ali Hemen

sentences.zh: 阿離合懣，景祖第八子也。

translations.literal: Ali Hemen was the eighth son of Emperor Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: Ali Hemen was the eighth son of the Jing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 健捷善戰。

translations.literal: He was robust, agile, and skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Vigorous and quick, he excelled in warfare.

sentences.zh: 年十八，臘醅、麻產起兵據暮棱水，烏春、窩謀罕以姑里甸兵助之。

translations.literal: At eighteen, Lapu and Machan raised troops and seized Muleng River; Wuchun and Wamohan aided them with Golidian forces.
translations.idiomatic: When he was eighteen, Lapu and Machan rebelled and held the Muleng River; Wuchun and Wamohan supported them with troops from Golidian.

sentences.zh: 世祖擒臘醅，暮棱水人尚反側，不自安，使阿離合懣往撫差之，與斜缽合兵攻窩謀罕。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor captured Lapu; the people of Muleng River still wavered and were uneasy, so he sent Ali Hemen to reassure and pacify them, and together with Xiebo he joined forces to attack Wamohan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shizu Emperor captured Lapu, the people along the Muleng River remained unsettled; he sent Ali Hemen to reassure them and, joining with Xiebo, attacked Wamohan.

sentences.zh: 烏春已死，窩謀罕棄城遁去。

translations.literal: Wuchun was already dead; Wamohan abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchun was already dead, and Wamohan abandoned his stronghold and fled.

sentences.zh: 後從撒改討平留可，阿離合懣功居多。

translations.literal: Later he followed Sagai in suppressing Liuke; Ali Hemen's achievements were the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following Sagai in the campaign to pacify Liuke, Ali Hemen contributed the lion's share of the credit.

sentences.zh: 太祖擒蕭海里，使阿離合懣獻馘於遼。

translations.literal: When the Taizu captured Xiao Haili, he had Ali Hemen present the severed heads to Liao.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu captured Xiao Haili, he sent Ali Hemen to present the enemy heads to the Liao court.

sentences.zh: 太祖謀伐遼，阿離合懣實贊成之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu planned to attack Liao, Ali Hemen truly supported it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu planned the campaign against Liao, Ali Hemen was a firm advocate.

sentences.zh: 及舉兵，阿離合懣在行間屢戰有功。

translations.literal: When troops were raised, Ali Hemen fought repeatedly in the ranks with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army marched, Ali Hemen fought again and again at the front and won repeated distinction.

sentences.zh: 及太宗等勸進，太祖未之許也。

translations.literal: When Taizong and others urged him to take the throne, the Taizu had not yet agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong and others pressed him to assume the throne, the Taizu still held back.

sentences.zh: 阿離合懣、昱、宗翰等曰：「今大功已集，若不以時建號，無以系天下心。

translations.literal: Ali Hemen, Yu, Zonghan, and others said: "Great achievements are now gathered; if we do not establish a title in season, there is no way to bind the hearts of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ali Hemen, Yu, Zonghan, and the others said, "Our great enterprise is complete; if we do not proclaim a reign title now, we cannot hold the hearts of the realm.

sentences.zh: 〕太祖曰：「吾將思之。」

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "I shall consider it."
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu replied, "I will think on it."

sentences.zh: 收國元年，太祖即位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shouguo, the Taizu took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shouguo (1115), the Taizu ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 阿離合懣與宗翰以耕具九為獻，祝曰：「使陛下毋忘稼穡之艱難。」

translations.literal: Ali Hemen and Zonghan presented nine farming implements as tribute, praying: "May Your Majesty not forget the hardships of tillage and harvest."
translations.idiomatic: Ali Hemen and Zonghan presented nine farming tools as a gift, with the prayer: "May Your Majesty never forget how hard it is to raise the crops."

sentences.zh: 太祖敬而受之。

translations.literal: The Taizu received them with respect.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu received them with reverence.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為國論乙室勃極烈。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he became Guolun Yishi Bojilie.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Guolun Yishi Bojilie.

sentences.zh: 為人聰敏辨給，凡一聞見，終身不忘。

translations.literal: As a man he was clever, quick-witted, and eloquent; whatever he heard or saw once, he never forgot for life.
translations.idiomatic: Clever, articulate, and quick on his feet, he never forgot anything he heard or saw even once.

sentences.zh: 始未有文字，祖宗族屬時事並能默記，與斜葛同修本朝譜牒。

translations.literal: At first there was no writing; he could memorize by heart the affairs of the imperial clan and kin, and together with Xiege he compiled the genealogical registers of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In the days before there was a written script, he could recite from memory the affairs of the imperial clan; with Xiege he compiled the dynasty's genealogical records.

sentences.zh: 見人舊未嘗識，聞其父祖名，即能道其部族世次所出。

translations.literal: Seeing someone he had never met before, once he heard the names of father and grandfather he could state from which tribe and generation they came.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting a stranger for the first time, he needed only to hear the names of the man's father and grandfather to trace his clan, generation, and lineage.

sentences.zh: 或積年舊事，偶因他及之，人或遺忘，輒一一辨析言之，有質疑者皆釋其意義。

translations.literal: Or matters of many years past—if someone else happened to mention them and people had forgotten, he would analyze and speak of them one by one; those who questioned him he would all satisfy as to their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: On some long-past matter that others had forgotten, if it came up in conversation he would lay out each point in order and clear up every doubt.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗稱其強記，人不可及也。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor once praised his powerful memory, saying no one could match him.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu Emperor once said that his memory was beyond anyone else's reach.

sentences.zh: 天輔三年，寢疾，宗翰日往問之，盡得祖宗舊俗法度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu he took to his bed with illness; Zonghan visited him daily and fully obtained the old customs and laws of the forefathers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianfu (1119) he fell ill; Zonghan visited him every day and learned from him the full body of ancestral custom and law.

sentences.zh: 疾病，上幸其家問疾，問以國家事，對曰：「馬者甲兵之用，今四方未平，而國俗多以良馬殉葬，可禁止之。」

translations.literal: During his illness the emperor visited his home to inquire after him and asked about state affairs; he replied: "Horses are the use of armor and weapons; the four quarters are not yet pacified, yet by national custom many fine horses are buried in sacrifice—this may be forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor came to his home to inquire after him and asked about affairs of state, he answered, "Horses are the sinews of war. The realm is not yet settled, yet our custom buries many fine horses with the dead—that practice should be stopped."

sentences.zh: 乃獻平生所乘戰馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he presented the war horses he had ridden all his life.
translations.idiomatic: He then presented the war horses he had ridden throughout his life.

sentences.zh: 及以馬獻太宗，使其子蒲里迭代為奏，奏有誤語，即哂之，宗翰從傍為改定。

translations.literal: When he presented horses to Taizong, he had his son Pulidai act as presenter; the presentation had erroneous wording, and he at once sneered at him; Zonghan standing by corrected and fixed it.
translations.idiomatic: When he presented horses to Taizong, he had his son Pulidai deliver the memorial; Pulidai misspoke, and he laughed at him on the spot while Zonghan, standing beside him, corrected the wording.

sentences.zh: 進奏訖，薨，年四十九。

translations.literal: When the presentation was finished, he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the presentation was done, he died, at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 上聞阿離合懣臨薨有奏事，曰：「臨終不亂，念及國家事，真賢臣也。」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard that Ali Hemen on his deathbed had presented memorial business, he said: "Unruffled at the end, mindful of state affairs—a true worthy minister."
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Ali Hemen had presented state business on his deathbed, the emperor said, "Composed to the last and thinking of the realm—he was a true worthy minister."

sentences.zh: 哭之慟。

translations.literal: He wept for him bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned him with deep grief.

sentences.zh: 及葬，上親臨。

translations.literal: At the burial the emperor came in person.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral the emperor attended in person.

sentences.zh: 熙宗時，追封隋國王。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xizong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xizong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Sui.

sentences.zh: 天德中，改贈開府儀同三司、隋國公。

translations.literal: In the Tiande era he was changed to be granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi and Duke of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiande period his posthumous honors were raised to Grand Preceptor of the Palace with the rank of Duke of Sui.

sentences.zh: 大定間，配饗太祖廟廷，諡曰剛憲。

translations.literal: In the Dading period he was granted co-sacrifice in the Taizu temple hall; his posthumous name was Gangxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dading era he was given a place in the sacrifices at the Taizu temple, with the posthumous title Gangxian (Steadfast and Law-abiding).

sentences.zh: 子賽也、斡論。

translations.literal: His sons were Saiye and Wolun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Saiye and Wolun.

sentences.zh: 賽也子宗尹。

translations.literal: Saiye's son was Zongyin.
translations.idiomatic: Saiye's son was Zongyin.

sentences.zh: 子 晏

translations.literal: Son: Yan
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan

sentences.zh: 晏本名斡論，景祖之孫，阿離合懣次子也。

translations.literal: Yan, original name Wolun, was a grandson of Emperor Jingzu and the second son of Ali Hemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, whose original name was Wolun, was a grandson of the Jing Emperor and the second son of Ali Hemen.

sentences.zh: 明敏多謀略，通契丹字。

translations.literal: Bright, keen, and full of stratagems; he knew Khitan script.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-minded and resourceful, he was versed in the Khitan script.

sentences.zh: 天會初，烏底改叛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhui, the Udige rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianhui era (1123), the Udige tribes rebelled.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸北京，以晏有籌策，召問，稱旨，乃命督扈從諸軍往討之。

translations.literal: Taizong visited the Northern Capital; because Yan had plans and stratagems, he summoned and questioned him; it matched the emperor's intent, and he then ordered him to supervise the accompanying armies to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong went to the Northern Capital, he summoned Yan for his counsel; pleased with his answers, he put him in command of the imperial escort forces sent to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 至混同江，諭將士曰：「今叛眾依山谷，地勢險阻，林木深密，吾騎卒不得成列，未可以歲月破也。」

translations.literal: Reaching the Huntong River, he instructed the officers and soldiers: "The rebels now rely on mountain valleys; the terrain is perilous and obstructed, the woods deep and dense; our cavalry and infantry cannot form ranks—it cannot be broken in months."
translations.idiomatic: At the Huntong River he told his officers, "The rebels have taken to the hills; the ground is steep and the forest thick. Our horsemen cannot fight in formation, and this will not be settled in a matter of months."

sentences.zh: 乃具舟楫艤江，令諸軍據高山，連木為柵，多張旗幟，示以持久計，聲言俟大軍畢集而發。

translations.literal: Thereupon he prepared boats and moored them on the river, ordered the armies to hold the high mountains, linked timbers into palisades, displayed many banners and flags to show a plan of endurance, and proclaimed that they would wait until the great army was fully gathered before setting out.
translations.idiomatic: He fitted out boats and anchored them on the river, posted his troops on the heights, linked timbers into palisades, and raised many banners to suggest a long siege, announcing that he would strike only when the main force had fully assembled.

sentences.zh: 乃潛以舟師浮江而下，直搗其營，遂大破之，據險之眾不戰而潰。

translations.literal: Then secretly he sent the fleet downstream on the river, struck straight at their camp, and greatly defeated them; the masses holding the defiles fled without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Then, under cover of night, he sent his fleet downstream and struck their camp head-on; the rebels in the defiles broke and fled without a fight.

sentences.zh: 月餘，一境皆定。

translations.literal: Within a month more the whole region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within little more than a month the entire region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 師還，授左監門衛上將軍，為廣甯尹，入為吏、禮兩部尚書。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed Left Supervisor of the Gate Guards Senior General, made Guangning Yin, and entered the capital as Minister of both Personnel and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Senior General of the Left Gate Guards, appointed Guangning Yin, and later served as Minister of Personnel and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 大定二年正月，上如山陵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Dading, the emperor went to the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Dading (1162), the emperor went to the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，上將獵，有司已夙備。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished the emperor was about to hunt; the officials had long since made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites were complete the emperor was about to go hunting; the officials had already made ready.

sentences.zh: 晏諫曰：「邊事未甯，畋遊非所宜也。」

translations.literal: Yan remonstrated: "Border affairs are not yet settled; hunting excursions are not appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Yan remonstrated, "The frontier is not yet secure; this is no time for the hunt."

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed his advice.

sentences.zh: 因謂晏等曰：「古者帝王虛心受諫，朕常慕之。

translations.literal: He then said to Yan and the others: "Ancient emperors and kings received remonstrance with an open mind; I have always admired this.
translations.idiomatic: He then told Yan and the others, "The sage kings of old listened humbly to remonstrance; I have always admired that.

sentences.zh: 卿等盡言毋隱。」

translations.literal: You all speak fully and do not conceal."
translations.idiomatic: Speak your minds freely and hold nothing back."

sentences.zh: 進拜太尉。

translations.literal: He was advanced and appointed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was promoted to Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 複致仕，還鄉里。

translations.literal: He again retired from office and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He retired once more and returned to his home.

sentences.zh: 是歲，薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died.

sentences.zh: 詔有司致祭，賻贈銀幣甚厚。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the officials to perform sacrifices; funeral gifts of silver and goods were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the proper rites of mourning, with a lavish grant of silver and goods.

sentences.zh: 孫 宗尹

translations.literal: Grandson: Zongyin
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zongyin

sentences.zh: 宗尹，本名阿里罕。

translations.literal: Zongyin, original name Alihan.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyin, whose original name was Alihan.

sentences.zh: 以宗室子充護衛，改牌印祗候，授世襲謀克，為右衛將軍。

translations.literal: As a son of the imperial clan he served as guard; he was changed to seal-and-register attendant, granted a hereditary mouke, and made Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: As a member of the imperial clan he first served in the guard corps, then became a seal-and-register attendant; he received a hereditary mouke and was appointed Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 曆順天、歸德、彰化、唐古部族、橫海軍節度使。

translations.literal: He successively served as military governor of Shuntian, Guide, Zhanghua, Tanggu tribal district, and Henghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Shuntian, Guide, and Zhanghua, as commissioner over the Tanggu tribes, and as military governor of the Henghai circuit.

sentences.zh: 正隆南伐，領神略軍都總管，先鋒渡淮，取揚州及瓜洲渡。

translations.literal: On the southern campaign of Zhenglong he led the Shenlue Army as supreme commander; as vanguard he crossed the Huai, took Yangzhou and Guazhou crossing.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign of the Zhenglong era (1158–1161) he commanded the Shenlue Army as supreme commander; leading the vanguard he crossed the Huai, seized Yangzhou, and took the Guazhou crossing.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，改河南路副都統，駐軍許州之境。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was changed to Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Henan Route, stationing troops in the territory of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he was made Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Henan Route and encamped his forces in the Xuzhou region.

sentences.zh: 是時，宋陷汝州，殺刺史烏古孫麻潑及漢軍二千人。

translations.literal: At this time Song captured Ruzhou, killing the prefect Wugusun Mapo and two thousand Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Song seized Ruzhou and killed the prefect Wugusun Mapo along with two thousand Han troops.

sentences.zh: 宗尹遣萬戶孛術魯定方、完顏阿喝懶、夾穀清臣、烏古論三合、渠雛訛只將騎四千往攻之，遂複取汝州。

translations.literal: Zongyin sent the ten-thousand-commanders Shulü Dingfang, Wanyan Ahalan, Jiagu Qingchen, Wugulun Sanhe, and Qu Chuozhi leading four thousand horsemen to attack; they then recovered Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyin sent the commanders of ten thousand Shulü Dingfang, Wanyan Ahalan, Jiagu Qingchen, Wugulun Sanhe, and Qu Chuozhi with four thousand cavalry to retake it, and Ruzhou was recovered.

sentences.zh: 除大名尹，副統如故。

translations.literal: He was removed to be Daming Yin, his deputy commandership unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Daming Yin while retaining his post as deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為河南路統軍使，遷元帥左都監，除南京留守。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he became Commander-in-Chief of the Henan Route, was transferred to Left Supervisor of the Marshals, and appointed Nanjing Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became Commander-in-Chief of the Henan Route, was transferred to Left Supervisor of the Marshals, and was appointed Garrison Commander of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿年少壯，而心力多滯。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are young and vigorous, yet your mental powers are much obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are still young and strong, yet your mind too often grows sluggish.

sentences.zh: 前任點檢京尹，勤力不怠，而處事迷錯。

translations.literal: In your previous post as Metropolitan Inspector and Capital Yin you were diligent and tireless, yet in handling affairs you were confused and mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: As Metropolitan Inspector and Capital Yin you worked tirelessly, yet you often blundered in your decisions.

sentences.zh: 勉修職業，以副朕意。」

translations.literal: Strive to cultivate your duties to match my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Apply yourself to your office and live up to what I expect of you."

sentences.zh: 賜通犀帶、廄馬。

translations.literal: He was granted a rhinoceros-horn belt and stable horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a rhinoceros-horn belt and horses from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 八年，置山東路統軍司，宗尹為使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Shandong Route Commander-in-Chief office was established; Zongyin was made its commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1168) the Shandong Route command was established, with Zongyin as its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遷樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 錄其父功，授世襲蒲與路屯河猛安，並親管謀克。

translations.literal: Recording his father's achievements, he was granted the hereditary Meng'an of Tunhe in Puyu Route and personally supervised moukes.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his father's service he was granted the hereditary meng'an of Tunhe in the Puyu Route and given personal charge of the moukes.

sentences.zh: 隊太子太保，樞密副使如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, his vice commissionership of the Privy Council unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent while retaining his post as Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 上問宰臣曰：「宗尹雖才無大過人者，而性行淳厚，且國之舊臣，昔為達官，卿等尚未仕也。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers: "Although Zongyin's talent does not greatly surpass others, his nature and conduct are pure and thick, and he is an old minister of the state; in the past he was a high official when you had not yet taken office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his chief ministers, "Zongyin is not a man of outstanding talent, but his character is honest and steady, and he is an elder servant of the state—he held high office when you had not yet entered service.

sentences.zh: 朕欲以為平章政事何如？」

translations.literal: I wish to make him Pingzhang Zhengshi—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to appoint him Grand Councilor—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 宰執皆曰：「宗尹為相，甚協眾望。」

translations.literal: The chief executives all said: "Zongyin as chancellor greatly accords with public expectation."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers all replied, "Zongyin as chancellor would satisfy the hopes of the realm."

sentences.zh: 即日拜平章政事，封代國公，兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed Pingzhang Zhengshi, enfeoffed as Duke of Dai, and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was appointed Grand Councilor, enfeoffed as Duke of Dai, and made concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是時民間苦錢幣不通，上問宗尹，對曰：「錢者有限之物，積於上者滯於下，所以不通。

translations.literal: At this time the people suffered because coin did not circulate; the emperor asked Zongyin, who replied: "Coin is a thing of limited quantity; what accumulates above stagnates below—that is why it does not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the people were distressed because currency would not circulate; when the emperor asked Zongyin, he answered, "Money is a finite commodity; when it piles up at the top it stagnates below—that is why it will not flow.

sentences.zh: 海陵軍興，為一切之賦，有菜園、房稅、養馬錢。

translations.literal: When Hailing raised armies, there were catch-all levies: vegetable-garden tax, house tax, and horse-keeping money.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing launched his wars he imposed blanket levies, including taxes on vegetable gardens and houses and a horse-keeping levy.

sentences.zh: 大定初，軍事未息，調度不繼，故因仍不改。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading military affairs had not ceased and allocations could not keep up, so they continued unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading the armies were still in the field and revenue could not keep pace, so these taxes were left in place.

sentences.zh: 今天下無事，府庫充積，悉宜罷去。」

translations.literal: Now the realm is without affairs, the treasuries full and stored—all should be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is at peace and the treasuries are full; all of them should be abolished."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿留意百姓，朕複何慮。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You attend to the common people—what further worry have I?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You have the people's welfare at heart—what more need I concern myself with?

sentences.zh: 太尉守道老矣，舍卿而誰。」

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal Shoudao is old; apart from you, who else?
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal Shoudao is old; if not you, then who?"

sentences.zh: 於是，養馬等錢始罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the horse-keeping money and the like were first abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the horse-keeping levy and similar imposts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 他日，上謂宰臣曰：「宗尹治家嚴密，他人不及也。」

translations.literal: Another day the emperor said to the chief ministers: "Zongyin governs his household with strict tightness—others cannot match him."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor told his ministers, "Zongyin runs his household with a discipline no one else can match."

sentences.zh: 顧謂宗尹曰：「政事亦當如此矣。」

translations.literal: Turning to Zongyin he said: "State affairs should also be like this."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Zongyin he added, "Your conduct of government should be the same."

sentences.zh: 有頃，北方歲饑，軍食不足，廷議輸粟賑濟。

translations.literal: Before long the north had a year of famine; military provisions were insufficient; the court debated transporting grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the north suffered famine and army rations ran short; the court debated shipping grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 或謂比雖不登，而舊積有餘，秋成在近，不必更勞輸挽，宗尹曰：「國家平時積粟，本以備凶歲也，必待秋成，則憊者眾矣。

translations.literal: Some said that although this year did not yield well, old stores were still ample and the autumn harvest was near—there was no need to trouble transport again; Zongyin said: "The state in normal times stores grain precisely to prepare for famine years; if we must wait for the autumn harvest, the exhausted will be many.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that although the harvest had failed, old stores were still adequate and the autumn crop was near, so there was no need for costly transport; Zongyin said, "The state hoards grain in normal times precisely for years like this; if we wait for the autumn harvest, many will already have perished.

sentences.zh: 人有捐瘠，其如防戍何。」

translations.literal: When people waste away to skin and bone, what of frontier defense and garrison?"
translations.idiomatic: If the people starve, how are we to man the frontier garrisons?"

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 宗尹乞令子銀術可襲其猛安，會太尉守道亦乞令其子神果奴襲其謀克。

translations.literal: Zongyin requested that his son Yinzhuke be allowed to inherit his meng'an; at the same time Grand Marshal Shoudao also requested that his son Shenguonu inherit his mouke.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyin asked that his son Yinzhuke be permitted to inherit his meng'an; at the same time Grand Marshal Shoudao asked that his son Shenguonu inherit his mouke.

sentences.zh: 凡承襲人不識女直字者，勒令習學。

translations.literal: As for heirs, those who did not know Jurchen script were compelled to study it.
translations.idiomatic: Any heir who could not read Jurchen script was ordered to learn it.

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「此二子，吾識其一習漢字，未習女直字。

translations.literal: Shizong said, "Of these two sons, I know one has studied Chinese characters but has not studied Jurchen script.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said, "Of these two sons, I know that one has studied Chinese characters but has not studied Jurchen script.

sentences.zh: 自今女直、契丹、漢字曾學其一者，即許承襲。」

translations.literal: From now on, whoever among Jurchen, Khitan, and Chinese script has learned any one of them shall be permitted to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, anyone who has learned at least one of Jurchen, Khitan, or Chinese script may inherit.

sentences.zh: 遂著於令。

translations.literal: This was then written into regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The rule was then entered into statute.

sentences.zh: 宗尹有疾，不能赴朝。

translations.literal: Zongyin was ill and could not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyin fell ill and could not attend court.

sentences.zh: 上問宰臣曰：「宗尹何為不入朝？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers, "Why does Zongyin not come to court?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his chief ministers, "Why does Zongyin not come to court?

sentences.zh: 太尉守道以疾對。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Shoudao answered that it was due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Shoudao replied that illness was the reason.

sentences.zh: 曰：「丞相志甯嘗言，'若詔遣征伐，所不敢辭。

translations.literal: He said, "Grand Councilor Zhining once said, 'If an imperial order sends me on campaign, I would not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Grand Councilor Zhining once said, 'If the throne orders me on campaign, I would not refuse.

sentences.zh: 宰相之職，實不敢當'。

translations.literal: The office of chancellor I truly dare not undertake.
translations.idiomatic: But the office of chancellor I truly dare not accept.

sentences.zh: 宗尹亦豈此意耶。」

translations.literal: Would Zongyin have such an intent?"
translations.idiomatic: Would Zongyin mean the same?"

sentences.zh: 二十四年，世宗將幸上京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, Shizong was about to visit the Supreme Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (1184) Shizong planned a visit to the Supreme Capital.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「臨潢、烏古里石壘歲皆不登，朕欲自南道往，三月過東京，謁太后陵寢，五月可達上京。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Linhuang and Wuguli Shilei have had poor harvests year after year; I wish to go by the southern route, pass through Dongjing in the third month to visit the empress dowager's tomb, and reach the Supreme Capital by the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Linhuang and Wuguli Shilei have failed harvest after harvest; I mean to travel by the southern route, pass through Dongjing in the third month to visit the empress dowager's tomb, and reach the Supreme Capital by the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 春月烏獸孳孕，東作方興，不必搜田講事，卿等以為何如？」

translations.literal: In spring birds and beasts breed, eastern farming is just rising—we need not conduct hunting maneuvers and war games; what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: In spring the birds and beasts are breeding and eastern farming is underway—there is no need for hunting drills and war games; what do you think?

sentences.zh: 宗尹曰：「南道歲熟，芻粟賤，宜如聖旨。」

translations.literal: Zongyin said, "The southern route had a good harvest and fodder grain is cheap; it fits the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyin said, "The southern route had a good harvest and fodder is cheap; that accords with Your Majesty's plan.

sentences.zh: 遂由南道往焉。

translations.literal: They then went by the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: They then traveled by the southern route.

sentences.zh: 世宗至上京，聞同簽大宗正事宗寧不能撫治上京宗室，宗室子往往不事生業。

translations.literal: When Shizong reached the Supreme Capital, he heard that Zong Ning, co-signatory of the Grand Imperial Clan office, could not govern the imperial clan at the Supreme Capital, and imperial clan sons often did not pursue livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong reached the Supreme Capital, he learned that Zong Ning, co-signatory of the Grand Imperial Clan office, could not keep order among the clan there, and many young clansmen neglected their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 上謂宗尹曰：「汝察其事，宜懲戒之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Zongyin, "You investigate this matter—it should be punished and admonished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Zongyin, "Look into this and discipline them as you see fit.

sentences.zh: 宗尹奏曰：「隨仕之子，父沒不還本土，以此多好遊蕩。」

translations.literal: Zongyin memorialized, "Sons who follow fathers in office, when the father dies do not return to their native place—because of this many drift in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyin reported, "Sons who accompany their fathers in office often stay on after the father dies instead of returning home, and for that reason many drift into idleness.

sentences.zh: 上命召還。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them recalled.

sentences.zh: 宴宗室于皇武殿，擊球為樂。

translations.literal: He feasted the imperial clan in the Huangwu Hall and played cuju for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted the imperial clan in the Huangwu Hall and played cuju for amusement.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「賞賜宗室，亦是小惠，又不可一概遷官，欲令諸局分收補，其間人材孰可者？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Rewarding the imperial clan is also a small favor, and we cannot promote them all indiscriminately; I wish to have the various bureaus recruit them to fill vacancies—among them whose talent is usable?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Handing out rewards to the clan is only a small kindness, and we cannot promote them all alike; I want the various offices to take them on as recruits—who among them has real ability?

sentences.zh: 宗尹對曰：「奉國斡准之子按出虎、豫國公昱之曾孫阿魯可任使。」

translations.literal: Zongyin replied, "Fengguo Wozhun's son Anchuhu and Prince of Yuguogong Yu's great-grandson Alu can be entrusted with service.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyin answered, "Fengguo Wozhun's son Anchuhu and the Yuguoguo prince Yu's great-grandson Alu are fit for service.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「度可任何職，更訪其餘以聞。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Estimate what office each can hold; inquire further about the rest and report.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Judge what post each can fill, and look into the others and report back.

sentences.zh: 詔以按出虎、阿魯為奉禦。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Anchuhu and Alu as palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Anchuhu and Alu palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，乞致仕。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1187) he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「此老不事事，從其請可也。」

translations.literal: Shizong said, "This old man does not busy himself with affairs—grant his request.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said, "This old man no longer throws himself into affairs—grant his request.

sentences.zh: 宰臣奏曰：「舊臣宜在左右。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers memorialized, "An old minister should be kept at one's side.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers urged, "A veteran minister should be kept close at hand.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「宰相總天下事，非養老之地。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The chancellor oversees all affairs under heaven—it is not a place for nurturing the aged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The chancellor oversees the realm—it is not a post for easing into old age.

sentences.zh: 若不堪其職，朕亦有愧焉。

translations.literal: If he cannot bear the office, I too would have reason for shame.
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot bear the burden of office, I too would have reason to feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 如賢者在朝，利及百姓，四方瞻仰，朕亦與其光美。」

translations.literal: If worthy men are in court, the benefit reaches the common people; the four quarters look up in admiration, and I too share in that radiance and honor.
translations.idiomatic: When worthy men serve at court, the people profit and the realm looks up in admiration—and I share in that glory.

sentences.zh: 宰臣無以對。

translations.literal: The chief ministers had nothing to reply.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers had no answer.

sentences.zh: 宗尹入謝。

translations.literal: Zongyin entered to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyin came in to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿久任外官，不聞有過失，但恨用卿稍晚，今精力似衰矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You long served in outer offices; I never heard of fault on your part, only regret that I employed you somewhat late—now your vigor seems faded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You served long in the provinces; I never heard a word against you, only that I used you rather late—and now your strength seems spent.

sentences.zh: 省事至煩，若勉留卿，則四方以朕為私，卿亦不自安也。」

translations.literal: Managing affairs is extremely troublesome; if I pressed to keep you, the four quarters would take me as partial, and you too would not be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The business of government is wearisome; if I pressed you to stay, the realm would call me partial and you would not be at ease either.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上問宗尹子：「汝父致仕，將居何所？」

translations.literal: Before long the emperor asked Zongyin's son, "Your father has retired—where will he live?
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the emperor asked Zongyin's son, "Your father is retiring—where will he live?

sentences.zh: 其子曰：「聚屬既多，不能複在京師。」

translations.literal: His son said, "Our kin are numerous and we cannot remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His son said, "Our kin are too many—we cannot stay on in the capital.

sentences.zh: 上遣使問宗尹曰：「朕欲留卿，時相從遊，卿子之言如此，今定何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to ask Zongyin, "I wish to keep you to accompany me in leisure at times; your son speaks thus—what is settled now?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an envoy to ask Zongyin, "I want you to stay so we may enjoy leisure together; your son says otherwise—what have you decided?

sentences.zh: 宗尹曰：「臣豈不欲在此，但餘閒之年，猶在輦下，恐聖主心困耳。

translations.literal: Zongyin said, "How could your servant not wish to remain here, but in the years of remaining leisure, still under the imperial carriage, I fear troubling the sage ruler's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyin said, "How could I not wish to remain, but in the years left to me, still under the imperial precinct, I fear wearying Your Majesty's heart.

sentences.zh: 既哀老臣不忍擯棄，時時得瞻望天顏，臣豈敢他往。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty pities an old minister and cannot bear to cast me away, that I may from time to time behold the heavenly countenance—how could your servant dare go elsewhere?
translations.idiomatic: Yet since Your Majesty pities an old servant and cannot bear to cast me off, that I may still from time to time behold your face—how could I go elsewhere?

sentences.zh: 鄉里故老無存者，雖到彼，尚將與誰遊乎。」

translations.literal: None of the old friends of my native place remain; even if I went there, with whom would I still wander?
translations.idiomatic: None of the old friends of my native place remain; even if I went home, with whom would I keep company?

sentences.zh: 於是賜甲第一區，凡宴集畋獵皆從焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted one first-rank residence; whenever there were feasts, hunts, and gatherings he accompanied them.
translations.idiomatic: He was then granted a first-rank residence, and at every feast, hunt, or gathering he accompanied the court.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1188) he died.

sentences.zh: 孫 宗甯

translations.literal: Grandson Zong Ning
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Zong Ning

sentences.zh: 宗甯本名阿土古，系出景祖，太尉阿離合懣之孫。

translations.literal: Zong Ning, original name Atugu, was descended from the Jing Emperor, grandson of Grand Marshal Ali Hemen.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ning, whose original name was Atugu, was descended from the Jing Emperor and was a grandson of Grand Marshal Ali Hemen.

sentences.zh: 性勤厚，有大志。

translations.literal: By nature diligent and steadfast, with great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: He was diligent and steadfast by nature and harbored great ambition.

sentences.zh: 起家為海陵征南都統，戰瓜洲渡，功最。

translations.literal: He began his career as Hailing's southern campaign commander-in-chief; at the battle of Guazhou Ford his merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Hailing's commander of the southern expedition; at the battle of Guazhou Ford his merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 曆祁州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，為會甯府路押軍萬戶，擢歸德軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, he was Collation Corps commander of ten thousand for the Huining Prefecture Route, then promoted to military commissioner of the Guide Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading (1162) he was commander of ten thousand for the Huining Prefecture Route, then promoted to military commissioner of the Guide Army.

sentences.zh: 時方旱蝗，守寧督民捕之，得死蝗一斗，給粟一斗，數日捕絕。

translations.literal: At the time drought and locusts struck; Zong Ning urged the people to catch them—one dou of dead locusts earned one dou of grain, and within days they were eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Drought and locusts struck at the time; Zong Ning had the people hunt locusts, paying one dou of grain for each dou of dead insects, and within days the plague was gone.

sentences.zh: 移鎮寧昌軍，改知臨潢府事，移天德軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command Ningchang Army, made prefect of Linhuang, then transferred to Tiande Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command Ningchang Army, appointed prefect of Linhuang, then moved to Tiande Army.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗謂宰臣曰：「宗甯智慮雖淺，然所至人皆愛之。」

translations.literal: Shizong once told the chief ministers, "Although Zong Ning's wisdom and planning are shallow, wherever he goes people love him.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong once told his ministers, "Zong Ning is not deep in counsel, yet wherever he goes the people love him.

sentences.zh: 即命為行軍右翼都統，為賀宋正旦使。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed right-wing commander of the field army and envoy to congratulate Song on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly made right-wing commander of the field army and envoy to congratulate the Song court on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部尚書，授隆州路和團猛安烈里沒世襲謀克。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of War and granted the hereditary meng'an of Longzhou Route Ho Group and mouke of Liemo.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of War and was granted the hereditary meng'an of the Longzhou Route Ho Group and the Liemo mouke.

sentences.zh: 出知大名府事，徙鎮利涉軍，俄同簽大睦親府事。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Daming, transferred to command Lishui Army, then shortly co-signatory of the Great Harmony and Kinship office.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Daming, then commanded Lishui Army, and soon became co-signatory of the Great Harmony and Kinship office.

sentences.zh: 宗寧多病，世宗欲以涼地處之，俾知咸平，詔以其子符寶郎畝為韓州刺史，以便養。

translations.literal: Zong Ning was often ill; Shizong wished to place him in a cool region and had him govern Xianping; an edict made his son Treasure-Seal Attendant Mu prefect of Hanzhou for convenient care.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ning was often ill; Shizong wished to place him in a cooler region and appointed him to Xianping, with an edict making his son, Treasure-Seal Attendant Mu, prefect of Hanzhou so he could be near his father.

sentences.zh: 無幾，入授同判大睦親府事，拜平章政事。

translations.literal: Before long he entered and was appointed associate judge of the Great Harmony office and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to court as associate judge of the Great Harmony office and was appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，薨。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingchang (1191) he died.

sentences.zh: 宗甯居家約儉如寒素，臨事明敏。

translations.literal: Zong Ning kept his household frugal as if poor, but in affairs was sharp and keen.
translations.idiomatic: At home Zong Ning lived as frugally as a poor scholar, yet in office he was sharp and decisive.

sentences.zh: 其鎮臨潢，鄰國有警，宗甯聞知乏糧，即出倉粟，令以牛易之，敵知得粟，即遁去。

translations.literal: When he held Linhuang, a neighboring state had an alarm; Zong Ning heard they lacked grain and at once released store grain, ordering exchange for cattle; the enemy learning they had obtained grain at once fled.
translations.idiomatic: While he held Linhuang, a neighboring state raised an alarm; learning they lacked grain, Zong Ning opened the granaries and let grain be traded for cattle, and when the enemy learned they had grain they withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 邊人以窩斡亂後，苦無牛，宗寧複令民入粟易牛，既而民得牛而倉粟倍於舊，其經畫如此。

translations.literal: After the Woheluan disorder border people suffered greatly from lack of cattle; Zong Ning again had the people bring in grain to exchange for cattle; before long the people had cattle while store grain was double the former—such was his planning.
translations.idiomatic: After the Woheluan rebellion the frontier people were desperate for cattle; Zong Ning again had grain brought in to trade for oxen, and soon the people had cattle while the granaries held twice the grain they had before—such was his management.

sentences.zh: 宗道本名八十，上京司屬司人，系出景祖，太尉訛論之少子也。

translations.literal: Zong Dao, original name Bashi, man of the Shangjing subordinate bureau, descended from Jing Emperor, youngest son of Grand Marshal Eolun.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Dao, whose original name was Bashi, came from the Shangjing subordinate bureau, was descended from the Jing Emperor, and was the youngest son of Grand Marshal Eolun (Ali Hemen).

sentences.zh: 通《周易》、《孟子》，善騎射，大定五年，充閤門祗候，累除近侍局使。

translations.literal: He mastered the Book of Changes and Mencius, excelled at mounted archery; in the fifth year of Dading he served as door usher, and was repeatedly promoted to commissioner of the close attendance bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Book of Changes and Mencius and excelled at mounted archery; in the fifth year of Dading (1165) he became a gate usher and was repeatedly promoted to commissioner of the close attendance bureau.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，為賀宋正旦使，尋授河南路統軍使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Cheng'an he was envoy to congratulate Song on New Year's Day, then appointed commander-in-chief of Henan Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Cheng'an (1197) he was envoy to congratulate the Song on New Year's Day, then was made commander-in-chief of the Henan Route.

sentences.zh: 泗州民張偉獲宋人王萬，言彼界事情，宗道疑其冤，乃廉問得實。

translations.literal: Sizhou commoner Zhang Wei captured Song man Wang Wan, reporting affairs on their side; Zong Dao suspected injustice and investigated, learning the truth.
translations.idiomatic: A Sizhou commoner named Zhang Wei seized a Song man named Wang Wan and reported on affairs across the border; Zong Dao suspected a frame-up, investigated, and found the truth.

sentences.zh: 萬，楚州賈人，偉負萬貨五千餘貫，三年不償，萬理索，為偉所誣。

translations.literal: Wan was a merchant of Chuzhou; Wei owed Wan more than five thousand strings of goods and for three years did not repay; Wan went to claim by reason and was slandered by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was a merchant of Chuzhou; Wei owed him more than five thousand strings in goods and for three years refused payment; when Wan pressed his claim, Wei denounced him.

sentences.zh: 乃坐偉而歸萬，時人服其明。

translations.literal: Wei was then punished and Wan returned; people of the time admired his clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was punished and Wan was sent home; people of the time admired his discernment.

sentences.zh: 後乞至仕，朝廷知非本心，改知河中府，有惠政，民立像於層觀，以時祭之。

translations.literal: Later he requested retirement; the court knew it was not his true intent and made him prefect of Hezhong; he had benevolent administration, and the people erected his image on a tiered pavilion and sacrificed to it on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked to retire; the court knew his heart was not in leaving and made him prefect of Hezhong instead, where his rule brought real benefit and the people set up his image in a towered hall and offered seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 移知臨洮，以病解。

translations.literal: He was transferred to govern Linzhou, then resigned due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Linzhou, then stepped down because of illness.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe (1204) he died.

sentences.zh: 贈龍虎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 宗雄本名謀良虎，康宗長子。

translations.literal: Zong Xiong, original name Mou Lianghu, eldest son of Prince Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong, whose original name was Mou Lianghu, was the eldest son of Prince Kang.

sentences.zh: 其始生也，世祖見而異之，曰：「此兒風骨非常，他日必為國器。」

translations.literal: At his birth the Shizu Emperor saw him and marveled, saying, "This child's bearing is extraordinary; one day he will be the state's vessel.
translations.idiomatic: At his birth the Shizu Emperor saw him and was struck by him, saying, "This boy's bearing is extraordinary; one day he will be the state's pillar.

sentences.zh: 因解佩刀，使常置其側，曰：「俟其成人則使佩之。」

translations.literal: He therefore removed his belt knife and had it always placed at his side, saying, "When he reaches manhood have him wear it.
translations.idiomatic: He took off his belt knife and had it kept always at the boy's side, saying, "When he comes of age, let him wear it.

sentences.zh: 九歲能射逸兔。

translations.literal: At nine he could shoot a fleeing hare.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he could bring down a running hare.

sentences.zh: 年十一，射中奔鹿。

translations.literal: At eleven he shot a running stag.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he shot a running stag.

sentences.zh: 世祖坐之膝上曰：「兒幼已然，異已出倫輩矣。」

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor seated him on his knee and said, "The boy is already thus while young—his difference has exceeded his peers.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu Emperor set him on his knee and said, "Even as a child he is like this—he already stands above his peers.

sentences.zh: 以銀酒器賜之。

translations.literal: He was granted silver wine vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He was given silver wine vessels.

sentences.zh: 既長，風表奇偉，善談辯，多智略，孝敬謙謹，人愛敬之。

translations.literal: When grown, his bearing was marvelously imposing; skilled in debate, rich in strategy; filial, respectful, and modest—people loved and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was imposing in bearing, skilled in debate and rich in stratagem, filial and modest—men loved and honored him.

sentences.zh: 康宗沒，遼使阿息保來，乘馬至靈帷階下，擇取賵贈之馬。

translations.literal: When Prince Kang died, Liao envoy Axibao came, rode his horse to the foot of the mourning screen, and chose and took horses from the funeral gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kang died, the Liao envoy Axibao came, rode his horse to the foot of the mourning bier, and picked out horses from among the funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，欲殺阿息保，宗雄諫，太祖乃止。

translations.literal: Taizu was enraged and wished to kill Axibao; Zong Xiong remonstrated, and Taizu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was furious and meant to kill Axibao, but Zong Xiong dissuaded him and Taizu desisted.

sentences.zh: 太祖將舉兵，宗雄曰：「遼主驕侈，人不知兵，可取也。

translations.literal: When Taizu was about to raise troops, Zong Xiong said, "The Liao ruler is arrogant and extravagant; the people know nothing of war—they can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was about to take up arms, Zong Xiong said, "The Liao ruler is arrogant and extravagant and his people know nothing of war—the realm can be taken.

sentences.zh: 不能擒一蕭海里，而我兵擒之。」

translations.literal: They could not capture a single Xiao Haili, yet our troops captured him.
translations.idiomatic: They could not take even Xiao Haili, yet our troops captured him.

sentences.zh: 太祖善其言。

translations.literal: Taizu approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu approved his counsel.

sentences.zh: 攻甯江州，渤海兵銳甚。

translations.literal: Attacking Ningjiang Prefecture, Bohai troops were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Ningjiang Prefecture the Bohai troops fought fiercely.

sentences.zh: 宗雄以所部敗渤海兵，以功授世襲千戶謀克。

translations.literal: Zong Xiong with his command defeated Bohai troops and for merit was granted hereditary commander of a thousand mouke.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong routed the Bohai with his command and for the merit was granted a hereditary commander-of-a-thousand mouke.

sentences.zh: 太祖敗遼兵於出河店，宗雄推鋒力戰，功多。

translations.literal: Taizu defeated Liao troops at Chuhedian; Zong Xiong pressed the van and fought fiercely, with much merit.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu defeated Liao forces at Chuhedian; Zong Xiong led the charge and fought hard, winning great distinction.

sentences.zh: 達魯古城之役，宗雄將右軍，身先士卒戰，遼兵當右軍者已卻，上命宗雄助左軍擊遼兵。

translations.literal: At the battle of Dalucheng, Zong Xiong commanded the right wing, fighting ahead of the soldiers; the Liao troops facing the right wing had already retreated, and the emperor ordered Zong Xiong to aid the left wing in striking Liao troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Dalucheng Zong Xiong commanded the right wing and fought ahead of his men; the Liao facing the right had already given way, and the emperor ordered him to reinforce the left and strike the Liao.

sentences.zh: 宗雄繞遼兵後擊之，遼兵遂大潰，乘勝逐北。

translations.literal: Zong Xiong circled behind the Liao troops and struck; Liao troops then collapsed in great rout, and pressing victory they pursued north.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong swung behind the Liao line and attacked; the Liao broke in rout and the victors pressed the pursuit northward.

sentences.zh: 日已暮，圍之。

translations.literal: The sun had already set, and they besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: By evening they had surrounded them.

sentences.zh: 黎明，遼兵突圍出，追殺至乙呂白石而還。

translations.literal: At dawn Liao troops broke out of the encirclement; pursuing and killing to Yilü Baishi they returned.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Liao broke out; the pursuers chased them to Yilü Baishi and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上撫其背曰：「朕有此子，何事不濟。」

translations.literal: The emperor stroked his back and said, "With such a son as this, what affair would not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor clapped his back and said, "With a son like this, what could fail?

sentences.zh: 以禦服賜之。

translations.literal: He was granted imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was given imperial robes.

sentences.zh: 及遼帝以七十萬眾至馳門，諸將皆曰：「遼軍勢甚盛，不宜速戰。」

translations.literal: When the Liao emperor came to Chimen with seven hundred thousand troops, the generals all said, "Liao forces are very strong—we should not fight swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor reached Chimen with seven hundred thousand men, the generals all said, "The Liao host is too strong—we should not fight at once.

sentences.zh: 宗雄曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zong Xiong said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 遼兵雖眾，而皆庸將，士卒惴惴，不足畏也。

translations.literal: Although Liao troops are many, all are mediocre generals; soldiers are fearful—there is nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Their numbers are great, but their commanders are mediocrity itself and the soldiers are timid—there is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 戰則破之掌握間耳。」

translations.literal: Fight and they will be broken in the palm of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Strike now and we will crush them in our hands.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said.

sentences.zh: 追及遼帝于護步荅岡。

translations.literal: They pursued and overtook the Liao emperor at Hubudá Gang.
translations.idiomatic: They overtook the Liao emperor at Hubudá Gang.

sentences.zh: 宗雄率眾直前，短兵接。

translations.literal: Zong Xiong led the masses straight forward, closing at close quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong drove straight in at the head of his men and closed at close quarters.

sentences.zh: 宗雄令前行持挺擊遼兵馬首，後行者射之，大敗遼兵。

translations.literal: Zong Xiong ordered the vanguard to wield cudgels and strike Liao horses' heads; those behind shot them, greatly defeating Liao troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong ordered the vanguard to club the Liao horses' heads while the rear ranks shot the riders, and the Liao were routed.

sentences.zh: 上嘉宗雄功，執其手勞之，以禦介胄及禦戰馬、寶貨、奴婢賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Zong Xiong's merit, took his hand and comforted him, and granted imperial armor, imperial war horses, treasures, and slaves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his achievement, took his hand in congratulation, and gave him imperial armor and horses, treasures, and attendants.

sentences.zh: 斜也攻春州，宗雄與宗幹、婁室取金山縣。

translations.literal: Xie Ye attacked Chunzhou; Zong Xiong with Zong Gan and Loushi took Jinshan County.
translations.idiomatic: While Xie Ye attacked Chunzhou, Zong Xiong joined Zong Gan and Loushi in taking Jinshan County.

sentences.zh: 行近白鷹林，獲候者七人，縱其一人使歸。

translations.literal: Marching near Baiying Forest, they captured seven scouts and released one to return.
translations.idiomatic: Near Baiying Forest they seized seven scouts and sent one back as a messenger.

sentences.zh: 縣人聞大軍至，乃潰，遂下金山縣。

translations.literal: County people hearing the great army had arrived then collapsed; they then took Jinshan County.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the army was upon them, the county militia scattered and Jinshan fell.

sentences.zh: 與斜也俱取泰州。

translations.literal: Together with Xie Ye they took Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Xie Ye they took Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖自將取臨潢府，遣宗雄先啟行，遇遼兵五千，宗雄與戰，大軍亦至，大破之。

translations.literal: Taizu personally led the taking of Linhuang Prefecture, sent Zong Xiong to go ahead first; encountering five thousand Liao troops, Zong Xiong fought them; the great army also arrived and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu led the assault on Linhuang himself and sent Zong Xiong ahead; he met five thousand Liao troops, fought them until the main force arrived, and together they crushed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 及留守撻不野降，上以其女與宗雄，賞其啟行破遼援兵之功也。

translations.literal: When the defending commander Tabuye surrendered, the emperor gave his daughter to Zong Xiong, rewarding his merit in going ahead and breaking Liao relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison commander Tabuye surrendered, the emperor gave him Tabuye's daughter in marriage, rewarding Zong Xiong for clearing the Liao relief force on the advance.

sentences.zh: 既而與蒲家奴按視泰州地土，宗雄包其土來奏曰：「其土如此，可種植也。」

translations.literal: Soon after, with Pujianu he inspected Taizhou land; Zong Xiong wrapped its soil and came to memorialize, saying, "Its soil is thus—it can be planted."
translations.idiomatic: He then inspected the soil of Taizhou with Pujianu; Zong Xiong brought a sample wrapped in cloth and reported, "The land is like this—it will support cultivation."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 由是徙萬餘家屯田泰州，以宗雄等言其地可種藝也。

translations.literal: From this more than ten thousand households were moved to garrison-farm at Taizhou, because Zong Xiong and others said its land could be planted.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand households were then relocated to farm Taizhou on the strength of Zong Xiong's report that the land would bear crops.

sentences.zh: 西京既降複叛，時糧餉垂盡，議欲罷攻。

translations.literal: Western Capital having surrendered again rebelled; at the time provisions were nearly exhausted; discussion wished to abandon the attack.
translations.idiomatic: After the Western Capital had surrendered it rebelled again; provisions were running out and some urged abandoning the siege.

sentences.zh: 宗雄曰：「西京，都會也，若委而去之，則降者離心，遼之餘黨與夏人得以窺伺矣。」

translations.literal: Zong Xiong said, "Western Capital is a great metropolis; if we abandon and leave it, then those who surrendered will lose heart, and Liao remnants and Xia people will be able to spy and wait."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong said, "The Western Capital is a great metropolis; if we walk away, the surrendered will lose heart and Liao holdouts and the Xia will watch for openings."

sentences.zh: 乃立重賞以激士心。

translations.literal: They then established heavy rewards to stir soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rewards were offered to rally the troops.

sentences.zh: 既而，夜中有火，大如鬥，墜於城中。

translations.literal: Soon after, in the night there was fire, large as a bushel measure, falling within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Then one night a fireball the size of a bushel measure fell inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 宗雄曰：「此城破之象也。」

translations.literal: Zong Xiong said, "This is an omen of the city's breaking."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong said, "This is a sign that the city will fall."

sentences.zh: 及克西京，賜宗雄黃金百兩，衣十襲及奴婢等。

translations.literal: When Western Capital was taken, he was granted one hundred liang of yellow gold, ten suits of clothing, and slaves and the like.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Capital fell he was rewarded with a hundred liang of gold, ten suits of robes, and attendants.

sentences.zh: 與宗翰等擊耿守忠兵七千於西京之東四十里，大破之。

translations.literal: With Zong Han and others he struck Geng Shouzhong's seven thousand troops forty li east of the Western Capital and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Zong Han and others in routing Geng Shouzhong's seven thousand men forty li east of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 迎謁太祖于鴛鴦濼，從至歸化州。

translations.literal: He went to welcome and meet Taizu at Yuanyang Marsh, and followed to Guihua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He met Taizu at Yuanyang Marsh and accompanied him to Guihua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，宗幹問所欲言。

translations.literal: His illness was severe; Zong Gan asked what he wished to say.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, Zong Gan asked if he had anything left to say.

sentences.zh: 宗雄曰：「國家大業既成，主上壽考萬年，肅清四方，死且無恨。」

translations.literal: Zong Xiong said, "The state's great enterprise is already accomplished; the sovereign's longevity ten thousand years; clearing the four quarters—death yet without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong said, "The great enterprise is won, our lord will live ten thousand years and pacify the four quarters—I can die without regret."

sentences.zh: 天輔六年，薨，年四十。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu he died; age forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Tianfu (1122), at forty.

sentences.zh: 太祖來問疾，不及見，哭之慟。

translations.literal: Taizu came to inquire of his illness but did not arrive in time to see him; he wept for him in deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu came to visit him but arrived too late; he wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 謂群臣曰：「此子謀略過人，臨陣勇決，少見其比。

translations.literal: He told the ministers, "This son's stratagems surpass others; facing battle he is brave and decisive—few have been seen to match him.
translations.idiomatic: He told his ministers, "In stratagem he had no peer, and in battle he was resolute—one seldom sees his like.

sentences.zh: 賻贈加等。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts and bestowals were increased in rank.
translations.idiomatic: His funeral honors were raised a grade.

sentences.zh: 詔合紮千戶駙馬石家奴護喪歸，葬於歸化州，仍於死所建佛寺。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the united meng'an thousand-household imperial son-in-law Shi Jianu to escort the bier home; he was buried at Guihua Prefecture, and still at the place of death a Buddhist temple was built.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the united-meng'an chief Shi Jianu to escort the bier home; he was buried at Guihua, and a Buddhist temple was raised at the place of his death.

sentences.zh: 宗雄好學嗜書，嘗從上獵，誤中流矢，而神色不變，恐上知之而罪及射者。

translations.literal: Zong Xiong loved learning and cherished books; once following the emperor on a hunt, he was mistakenly struck by a stray arrow, yet his expression did not change—fearing the emperor would know and punish the shooter.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong loved books and study. Once on a hunt with the emperor he was hit by a stray arrow but did not change expression, fearing that if Taizu learned of it the archer would be punished.

sentences.zh: 既拔去其矢，托疾歸家，臥兩月，因學契丹大小字，盡通之。

translations.literal: Having pulled out the arrow, he pleaded illness and returned home, lying two months; therein he studied Khitan great and small script and fully mastered them.
translations.idiomatic: After pulling out the shaft he pleaded illness, went home, and lay abed two months—time he used to master both forms of Khitan script.

sentences.zh: 凡金國初建，立法定制，皆與宗幹建白行焉。

translations.literal: All when the Jin state was first established, establishing laws and fixing regulations, were jointly proposed and carried out with Zong Gan.
translations.idiomatic: In the founding of the Jin state he and Zong Gan proposed and carried out the laws and institutions.

sentences.zh: 及與遼議和，書詔契丹、漢字，宗雄與宗翰、希尹主其事。

translations.literal: When treating peace with Liao, writing edicts in Khitan and Chinese characters, Zong Xiong with Zong Han and Xi Yin directed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When peace with Liao was negotiated and edicts written in Khitan and Chinese, Zong Xiong worked with Zong Han and Xi Yin at the writing.

sentences.zh: 而材武蹻捷，挽強射遠，幾三百步。

translations.literal: Yet in talent and martial prowess he was nimble and swift; drawing the strong bow and shooting far, nearly three hundred paces.
translations.idiomatic: In martial skill he was swift and strong: he could bend the heavy bow and shoot nearly three hundred paces.

sentences.zh: 嘗走馬射三麞，已中其二，複彎弓，馬蹶，躍而下，控弦如故，遂彀滿步射獲之。

translations.literal: Once riding at gallop he shot at three roe deer, having already hit two; again bending the bow, the horse stumbled—he leaped down; controlling the bowstring as before, he then fully drew the bow and stepping shot and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Once while cantering he shot at three roe deer and brought down two; as he bent the bow again his horse stumbled—he sprang down, drew as if nothing had happened, and on foot sent the third arrow home.

sentences.zh: 宗雄方逐兔，撻懶亦從後射之，已發矢，撻懶大呼曰：「矢及矣。」

translations.literal: Zong Xiong was just pursuing a hare when Tayan also shot from behind; having already loosed the arrow, Tayan shouted greatly, "The arrow has reached!"
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong was chasing a hare when Tayan shot from behind; as the arrow flew Tayan shouted, "It's coming!"

sentences.zh: 宗雄反顧，以手接其矢，就射兔，中之，其輕健如此。

translations.literal: Zong Xiong turned his head, caught the arrow with his hand, and thereupon shot at the hare, hitting it—such was his lightness and vigor.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Xiong glanced back, caught the arrow in his hand, then shot and hit the hare—such was his quickness.

sentences.zh: 天眷中，追封太師、齊國王。

translations.literal: In Tianjuan he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor and King of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianjuan (1138–1141) he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and King of Qi.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，加秦漢國王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande, he was advanced to King of Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande (1150) he was advanced to King of Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，改太傅、金源郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong, changed to Grand Tutor and Prince of Jinyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong (1157) his title became Grand Tutor, Prince of Jinyuan.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，追封楚王，諡威敏，配享太祖廟廷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, posthumously enfeoffed King of Chu, posthumous name Weimin, paired in sacrifice at Taizu's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading (1162) he was posthumously made King of Chu with the temple name Weimin and granted a place in Taizu's ancestral hall.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詔圖像于衍慶宮。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, an edict ordered his portrait at Yanging Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year (1175) an edict ordered his portrait placed in Yanging Palace.

sentences.zh: 子蒲魯虎、按荅海、阿鄰。

translations.literal: Sons: Puluhu, An Dahai, Alin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Puluhu, An Dahai, and Alin.

sentences.zh: 孫常春、胡里刺、胡刺、鶻魯、茶紮、怕八、訛出。

translations.literal: Grandsons: Changchun, Hulici, Huci, Gulü, Chazha, Paba, Echu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons included Changchun, Hulici, Huci, Gulü, Chazha, Paba, and Echu.

sentences.zh: 初，宗幹納宗雄妻，海陵銜之。

translations.literal: At first Zong Gan took Zong Xiong's wife; Hailing harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zong Gan had taken Zong Xiong's widow, and Hailing never forgave it.

sentences.zh: 及篡位，使宿直將軍晁霞、牌印閭山往河間，囚宗雄妻于府署，明日，與其子婦及常春兄弟、茶紮之子七人皆殺而焚之，棄其骨于濠水。

translations.literal: When he usurped the throne, he sent night-duty general Chao Xia and seal-keeper Lüshan to Hejian, imprisoned Zong Xiong's wife at the prefectural office; the next day, with his daughters-in-law and the Changchun brothers and Chazha's sons—seven persons—all were killed and burned, their bones cast into the Hao River.
translations.idiomatic: When he seized the throne he sent the night-duty general Chao Xia and the seal keeper Lüshan to Hejian, where they imprisoned Zong Xiong's widow in the prefectural yamen; the next day she, her daughters-in-law, Changchun and his brothers, and Chazha's sons—seven in all—were killed and burned, and their bones thrown into the Hao River.

sentences.zh: 大定十七年，詔有司收葬。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Dading, an edict ordered the relevant offices to collect and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Dading (1177) an edict ordered proper burial for the remains.

sentences.zh: 初，蒲魯虎襲猛安。

translations.literal: At first Puluhu inherited the meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Puluhu had first inherited the meng'an title.

sentences.zh: 蒲魯虎卒，贈金紫光祿大夫，子桓端襲之，官至金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When Puluhu died he was posthumously granted Jinzi Guanglu Grand Master; his son Huanduan inherited it, reaching office as Grand General of the Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Puluhu died he was posthumously made Jinzi Guanglu Grand Master; his son Huanduan inherited the post and rose to Grand General of the Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 桓端卒，子嫋頻未襲而死。

translations.literal: When Huanduan died, his son Niaopin had not yet inherited and died.
translations.idiomatic: Huanduan's son Niaopin died before he could inherit.

sentences.zh: 章宗命宗雄孫蒲帶襲之。

translations.literal: Zhangzong ordered Zong Xiong's grandson Pudai to inherit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong ordered Zong Xiong's grandson Pudai to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 蒲帶，大定末，累官同簽大睦親府事。

translations.literal: Pudai, at the end of Dading, accumulated offices as co-signatory of the Grand Imperial Kinship office.
translations.idiomatic: Pudai held successive posts and by the end of Dading was co-signatory of the Grand Imperial Kinship office.

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，初置九路提刑司，蒲帶為北京臨潢提刑使。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong ascended, the nine-circuit supervisory censorate was first established; Pudai was Bianjing Linhuang supervisory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong came to the throne he established the nine-route judicial commissioners; Pudai was made commissioner for Beijing (Linhuang).

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕初即位，憂勞萬民，每念刑獄未平，農桑未勉，吏或不循法度，以隳吾治。

translations.literal: An edict said, "I have newly ascended; I worry and labor for the myriad people; each time I think that criminal cases are not settled, farming and sericulture are not encouraged—officials perhaps do not follow law and measure, thereby destroying my governance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "Since my accession I have worried for the people: prisons are not cleared, farming is neglected, and some officials ignore the law and undermine my rule.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣使廉問，事難周悉。

translations.literal: The court sends envoys to investigate integrity; affairs are hard to be thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Court envoys on integrity missions cannot cover everything.

sentences.zh: 惟提刑勸農採訪之官，自古有之。

translations.literal: Only supervisory censors who encourage farming and gather reports—such offices have existed since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet supervisory officers who encourage farming and gather intelligence have existed since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今分九路專設是職，爾其盡心，往懋乃事。」

translations.literal: Now dividing nine circuits to specially establish this office—you must exhaust your hearts; go and strive in your affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Now nine routes each have such a post—devote yourselves fully to the charge."

sentences.zh: 自熙宗時，遣使廉問吏治得失。

translations.literal: From Xizong's time, envoys were sent to investigate official administration's gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xizong's reign the court had sent envoys to assess officials.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，凡數歲輒一遣黜陟之，故大定之間，郡縣吏皆奉法，百姓滋殖，號為小康。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended, every few years one dispatch for promotion and demotion—thus during Dading, commandery and county officials all observed law, common people multiplied, and it was called a modest peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent such missions every few years to promote or dismiss officers, so that under Dading local officials kept the law, the people prospered, and the age was called a modest peace.

sentences.zh: 或謂廉問使者，頗以愛憎立殿最，以問宰相。

translations.literal: Some said integrity envoys largely used love and hate to establish rankings; the matter was asked of the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Some complained that integrity envoys ranked officials by personal liking; the emperor asked the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 宰相曰：「臣等複為陛下察之。」

translations.literal: The chancellor said, "We subjects again will investigate for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor answered, "We shall look into this again for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 是以世宗嘗欲立提刑司而未果。

translations.literal: Therefore Shizong once wished to establish the supervisory censorate but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Shizong had wished to create the judicial commission but did not succeed in his day.

sentences.zh: 章宗追述先朝，遂于即位之初行之。

translations.literal: Zhangzong followed up the former court, and thus at the beginning of his accession carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong followed his forebears' intent and instituted it at the start of his reign.

sentences.zh: 及九路提刑使朝辭于慶和殿，上曰：「建立官制，當寬猛得中。

translations.literal: When the nine-circuit supervisory commissioners took court leave at Qinghe Hall, the emperor said, "Establishing official systems should obtain the mean between lenient and stern.
translations.idiomatic: When the nine route commissioners took leave at Qinghe Hall, the emperor said, "In building government, leniency and severity must be balanced.

sentences.zh: 凡軍民事相涉者，均平決遣，鈐束家人部曲，勿使沮擾郡縣事。

translations.literal: All matters where military and civilian affairs intersect—decide and dispatch with even balance; restrain household families and personal troops, do not let them obstruct and disturb commandery and county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Where civil and military matters overlap, judge fairly; restrain your households and retainers so they do not interfere with local government.

sentences.zh: 今以司獄隸提刑司，惟翼獄犴無冤耳。」

translations.literal: Now placing the prison office under the supervisory censorate—only wishing that prisons be without injustice."
translations.idiomatic: Prison affairs are now under your office—see only that no innocent languishes in the cells."

sentences.zh: 既退，複遣近臣諭之曰：「卿等皆妙簡才良，付以專責，盡心舉職，別有旌賞，否則有罰。」

translations.literal: Having withdrawn, again he sent close ministers to instruct them, saying, "You are all excellently selected talented and worthy; entrusted with specialized responsibility—exhaust your hearts in performing office; separately there will be rewards, otherwise there will be punishment."
translations.idiomatic: After they withdrew he sent a close minister to add: "You were chosen for talent and given a special charge—serve faithfully and you will be rewarded; fail and you will be punished."

sentences.zh: 明年，蒲帶乃襲猛安雲。

translations.literal: The next year Pudai then inherited the meng'an title.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Pudai inherited the meng'an.

sentences.zh: 子 阿鄰

translations.literal: Son: Alin
translations.idiomatic: Son: Alin

sentences.zh: 阿鄰，穎悟辯敏，通女直、契丹大小字及漢字。

translations.literal: Alin was quick-witted and eloquent, penetrating Jurchen, Khitan great and small script, and Chinese characters.
translations.idiomatic: Alin was sharp-witted and eloquent, fluent in Jurchen, both Khitan scripts, and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 幼時嘗入宮，熙宗見而奇之，曰：「是兒他日必能宣力國家。」

translations.literal: In youth he once entered the palace; Xizong saw him and marveled, saying, "This child in the future will surely be able to exert strength for the state."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he visited the palace; Xizong was impressed and said, "This boy will one day serve the state well."

sentences.zh: 年十八，授定遠大將軍，為順天軍節度使。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he was appointed General Who Settles the Distance and made military governor of Shuntian Army.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was made General Who Settles the Distance and military governor of the Shuntian army.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，用廉，遷益都尹兼山東東路兵馬都總管，曆泰寧、定海、鎮西、安國等軍節度。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande, through integrity-selection, he was transferred to Prefect of Yidu and concurrent commander-in-chief of Shandong Eastern Route forces, passing through Taining, Dinghai, Zhenxi, Anguo and other army governorships.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande (1150), through the integrity process, he became prefect of Yidu and concurrent commander of Shandong Eastern Route forces, and later held governorships at Taining, Dinghai, Zhenxi, Anguo, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 海陵南伐，以為神勇、武平等軍都總管，由壽州道渡淮，與勸農使移刺元宜合兵三萬為先鋒。

translations.literal: When Hailing southern-campaigned, he was made commander-in-chief of Shenyong and Wuping armies; by the Shouzhou route he crossed the Huai, and with farming-encouragement commissioner Yila Yuanyi united armies of thirty thousand as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In Hailing's southern campaign he commanded the Shenyong and Wuping armies, crossed the Huai by the Shouzhou route, and with the farming commissioner Yila Yuanyi led thirty thousand men as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，至廬州，與宋將王權軍十余萬戰於柘皋鎮，渭子橋，敗之。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month, reaching Luzhou, he with Song general Wang Quan's army of more than a hundred thousand fought at Zhegao town and Weizi Bridge and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: That October he reached Luzhou and at Zhegao and Weizi Bridge defeated Song general Wang Quan's army of more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 至和州南，複與王權軍八萬餘會戰，又敗之，追殺至江上，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Reaching south of Hezhou, again with Wang Quan's army of more than eighty thousand he joined battle and again defeated them, pursuing and killing to the river—severed heads several thousand grades.
translations.idiomatic: South of Hezhou he met Wang Quan's eighty thousand again, routed them, and chased them to the river, taking several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 子 按荅海

translations.literal: Son: An Dahai
translations.idiomatic: Son: An Dahai

sentences.zh: 按荅海，又名阿魯綰，宗雄次子也。

translations.literal: An Dahai, also named Aluqian, was Zong Xiong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: An Dahai, also called Aluqian, was Zong Xiong's second son.

sentences.zh: 性端重，不輕發，有父之風。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and grave, not lightly aroused—he had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: He was steady and reserved, with his father's bearing.

sentences.zh: 年十五，太祖賜以一品傘。

translations.literal: At age fifteen Taizu granted him a first-rank umbrella.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Taizu granted him a first-rank ceremonial umbrella.

sentences.zh: 二十餘，禦球場分朋擊球，連勝三算，宗工舊老鹹異之。

translations.literal: Past twenty, at the imperial cuju ground dividing sides and striking the ball, he won three bouts in succession; clan elders of the founding generation all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties, at a palace cuju match he won three bouts in a row and impressed the founding-generation elders.

sentences.zh: 進呈所勝禮物，按荅海為班首，太宗喜曰：「今日之勝，此孫之力也。」
