translations.literal: Presenting the victor's gifts, An Dahai was chief of the team; Taizong said with pleasure, "Today's victory is this grandson's strength."
translations.idiomatic: When the winners presented their gifts An Dahai led the team; Taizong said with pleasure, "Today's victory is this grandson's doing."

sentences.zh: 賞力獨厚。

translations.literal: Rewards to him alone were thick.
translations.idiomatic: His reward alone was especially generous.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，襲父猛安。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan he inherited his father's meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjuan (1139) he inherited his father's meng'an.

sentences.zh: 除大宗正丞，以猛安讓兄子喚端，加武定軍節度使，奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Clan office; giving up the meng'an to his elder brother's son Huanduan, he was advanced to military governor of Wuding Army as court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Grand Imperial Clan, yielded the meng'an to his brother's son Huanduan, and was promoted to military governor of Wuding with court attendance.

sentences.zh: 改侍衛親軍都指揮使，封金源郡王，進封譚王，遷同判大宗正事，別授世襲猛安。

translations.literal: Changed to Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard, enfeoffed Prince of Jinyuan Commandery, advanced to Prince of Tan, transferred to Co-Director of Grand Imperial Clan affairs, separately granted hereditary meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: He became commander of the Palace Guard, was made Prince of Jinyuan and then Prince of Tan, served as co-director of the Grand Imperial Clan, and received a separate hereditary meng'an.

sentences.zh: 海陵將遷中都，按荅海諫曰：「棄祖宗興王之地而他徙，非義也。」

translations.literal: When Hailing was about to move the capital to Zhongdu, An Dahai remonstrated, saying, "To abandon the place where forefathers raised the kingship and move elsewhere is not righteous."
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing planned to move the capital to Zhongdu, An Dahai remonstrated: "To abandon the land where our forefathers raised the dynasty is not right."

sentences.zh: 海陵不悅，留之上京。

translations.literal: Hailing was displeased and kept him at the Supreme Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing took offense and kept him at the Supreme Capital.

sentences.zh: 久之，進封鄆王，改封魏王，除濟南尹。

translations.literal: After long time, advanced to Prince of Yan, changed to Prince of Wei, appointed Prefect of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was advanced to Prince of Yan, then Prince of Wei, and made prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 按荅海不堪卑濕，多在病告，海陵聞之，改西京留守。

translations.literal: An Dahai could not bear low dampness and often took sick leave; when Hailing heard, he changed him to Western Capital defender.
translations.idiomatic: An Dahai could not endure Jinan's damp climate and was often on sick leave; when Hailing heard, he made him defender of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 正隆例奪王爵，改廣甯尹。

translations.literal: Under the Zhenglong precedent princely titles were stripped; he was changed to Prefect of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenglong purge of princes he lost his royal title and became prefect of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 海陵時，自上京徙河間，土瘠，詔按荅海一族二十五家，從便遷居近地，乃徙平州。

translations.literal: In Hailing's time, from the Supreme Capital they moved to Hejian; the soil was poor—an edict ordered An Dahai's clan of twenty-five households to move at convenience to a nearby place; they then moved to Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hailing, when the clan was moved from the Supreme Capital to Hejian the land proved barren; an edict let An Dahai's twenty-five households relocate as they chose, and they settled in Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔給平州官田三百頃，屋三百間，宗州官田一百頃。

translations.literal: An edict granted Pingzhou official fields three hundred qing, three hundred rooms, and Zongzhou official fields one hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted them three hundred qing of public land at Pingzhou, three hundred dwellings, and a hundred qing at Zongzhou.

sentences.zh: 進金源郡王，致仕。

translations.literal: Advanced to Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-made Prince of Jinyuan and retired.

sentences.zh: 大定八年，召見，上曰：「宗室耆老如卿者，能幾人邪。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dading he was summoned and seen; the emperor said, "Imperial clan elders like you—how many can there be?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dading (1168) he was summoned; the emperor said, "How many clan elders like you are left?"

sentences.zh: 賜錢萬貫，甲第一區，留京師，使預巡幸球獵宴會。

translations.literal: Granted ten thousand strings of cash, one first-rank residence; kept at the capital, made to participate in imperial tours, cuju, hunting, and banquets.
translations.idiomatic: He received ten thousand strings of cash and a mansion in the capital, and was invited to the emperor's tours, hunts, cuju matches, and banquets.

sentences.zh: 十四年，薨，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died; age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year (1174), at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 臨終，戒諸子曰：「汝輩勿以生富貴中而為暴戾，宜自謙退。

translations.literal: At life's end he admonished his sons, saying, "You must not because born in wealth and honor act violent and arrogant—you should yourselves be humble and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he warned his sons, "Do not grow arrogant because you were born to wealth and rank—stay humble.

sentences.zh: 海陵以猜忌剪滅宗室，我以純謹得免死耳。

translations.literal: Hailing through suspicion and jealousy cut down the imperial clan; I through pure caution alone escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing destroyed the clan through suspicion; I survived only by circumspection.

sentences.zh: 汝輩惟日為善，勿墜吾家。」

translations.literal: You must day by day do good—do not bring down our family."
translations.idiomatic: Do good every day and do not disgrace our house."

sentences.zh: 完顏希尹本名穀神，歡都之子也。

translations.literal: Wanyan Xi Yin, original name Gushen, was Huandu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Xi Yin, whose original name was Gushen, was the son of Huandu.

sentences.zh: 自太祖舉兵，常在行陣，或從太祖、或從撒改，或與諸將征伐，比有功。

translations.literal: From when Taizu raised troops he was always in the battle array—sometimes following Taizu, sometimes following Sagai, sometimes with various generals on campaigns—comparatively having merit.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizu's first campaigns he was always in the field—with Taizu, with Sagai, or with the other generals—and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 金人初無文字，國勢日強，與鄰國交好，乃用契丹字。

translations.literal: Jin people at first had no script; state power daily strengthened; treating with neighboring states in friendship, they then used Khitan script.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin at first had no writing of their own; as the state grew stronger and exchanged envoys with its neighbors, they adopted the Khitan script.

sentences.zh: 太祖命希尹撰本國字，備制度。

translations.literal: Taizu ordered Xi Yin to compose the national script, to complete institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu ordered Xi Yin to create a script for the Jin state and put government institutions on a written footing.

sentences.zh: 希尹乃依仿漢人楷字，因契丹字制度，合本國語，制女直字。

translations.literal: Xi Yin then modeled on Han regular script, following Khitan-script institutions, joined with the national language, and made Jurchen script.
translations.idiomatic: He took Han regular characters as a model, adapted the structure of the Khitan script, and fitted it to the Jurchen language to devise Jurchen writing.

sentences.zh: 天輔三年八月，字書成，太祖大悅，命頒行之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Tianfu, the book of characters was completed; Taizu was greatly pleased and ordered it promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Tianfu (1119) the primer was finished; Taizu was delighted and ordered it issued throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 賜希尹馬一匹、衣一襲。

translations.literal: He granted Xi Yin one horse and one suit of clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yin was rewarded with a horse and a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 其後熙宗亦制女直字，與希尹所制字俱行用。

translations.literal: Afterwards Xizong also made Jurchen script; both his script and Xi Yin's were used together.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xizong devised a Jurchen script as well, and both his and Xi Yin's systems came into use.

sentences.zh: 希尹所撰謂之女直大字，熙宗所撰謂之小字。

translations.literal: What Xi Yin composed was called the great Jurchen script; what Xizong composed was called the small script.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yin's creation was known as the "large" Jurchen script and Xizong's as the "small" script.

sentences.zh: 遼人迪六、和尚、雅里斯充中京走，希尹與迪古乃、婁室、餘睹襲之。

translations.literal: Liao men Di Liu, Heshang, and Yalisi fled from the Central Capital; Xi Yin with Digunai, Wushu, and Yudu struck at them.
translations.idiomatic: When Di Liu, Heshang, and Yalisi of Liao fled the Central Capital, Xi Yin joined Digunai, Wushu, and Yudu in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 迪六等聞希尹兵，複走。

translations.literal: When Di Liu and the others heard of Xi Yin's troops, they fled again.
translations.idiomatic: At news of Xi Yin's approach they fled once more.

sentences.zh: 遂降其旁近人民而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon they made the nearby people submit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They then secured the submission of the neighboring populace and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 奚人落虎來降，希尹使落虎招其父西節度使訛里刺。

translations.literal: Xi man Luohu came to surrender; Xi Yin had Luohu summon his father, the Western military commissioner Elili.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xi tribesman Luohu surrendered, Xi Yin sent him to win over his father Elili, military commissioner of the west.

sentences.zh: 訛里刺以本部降。

translations.literal: Elili surrendered with his command.
translations.idiomatic: Elili submitted with his entire command.

sentences.zh: 宗翰駐軍北安，使希尹經略近地，獲遼護衛耶律習泥烈，知遼主獵於鴛鴦濼。

translations.literal: Zong Han stationed troops at Bei'an and had Xi Yin manage nearby lands; he captured Liao guard Yelü Xini Lie and learned the Liao ruler was hunting at Yuanyang Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han encamped at Bei'an and sent Xi Yin to secure the surrounding country; from a captured Liao guard, Yelü Xini Lie, he learned that the Liao emperor was hunting at Yuanyang Marsh.

sentences.zh: 宗翰遂請進兵。

translations.literal: Zong Han then requested to advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han thereupon asked leave to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 宗翰將會都統杲于奚王嶺。

translations.literal: Zong Han was about to meet Commander-in-Chief Gao at Prince of Xi's Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han was to join Commander-in-Chief Gao at Prince of Xi's Ridge.

sentences.zh: 遼兵屯古北口。

translations.literal: Liao troops were encamped at Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: Liao forces held Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 使婆盧火將兵二百擊之，渾黜亦將二百人為後援。

translations.literal: He sent Poluhuo to lead two hundred troops to attack them; Hunchu also led two hundred men as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Poluhuo with two hundred men to strike them, with Hunchu and another two hundred in support.

sentences.zh: 渾黜聞遼兵眾，請益兵。

translations.literal: Hunchu heard the Liao troops were numerous and requested more troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hunchu, finding the Liao force large, asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 宗翰欲親往，希尹、婁室曰：「此小寇，請以千兵為公破之。」

translations.literal: Zong Han wished to go in person; Xi Yin and Wushu said: "These are petty bandits—please let a thousand troops break them for you."
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Han meant to lead the assault himself, Xi Yin and Wushu said, "This is a trifling enemy—give us a thousand men and we will rout them for you."

sentences.zh: 渾黜至古北口，遇遼遊兵，逐之入穀中。

translations.literal: Hunchu reached Gubeikou, met Liao skirmishers, and pursued them into a ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Hunchu reached Gubeikou, clashed with Liao scouts, and drove them into a defile.

sentences.zh: 遼步騎萬余迫戰，死者數人。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Liao infantry and cavalry pressed to battle; several men were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten thousand Liao foot and horse pressed the fight; a few Jin soldiers fell.

sentences.zh: 渾黜據關口，希尹等至，大破遼兵，斬馘甚眾，盡獲甲胄輜重。

translations.literal: Hunchu held the pass; when Xi Yin and the others arrived they greatly defeated the Liao army, beheaded many, and seized all armor and baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Hunchu held the pass until Xi Yin came up; together they shattered the Liao army, took many heads, and captured armor and wagons in full.

sentences.zh: 複敗其伏兵，殺千餘人，獲馬百餘匹。

translations.literal: They again defeated their ambush troops, killed more than a thousand, and captured over a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: They then broke an ambush, killing more than a thousand and taking over a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 遂與宗翰至奚王嶺，期會於羊城濼。

translations.literal: Then they joined Zong Han at Prince of Xi's Ridge, with a rendezvous set at Yangcheng Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: They rejoined Zong Han at Prince of Xi's Ridge and arranged to meet at Yangcheng Marsh.

sentences.zh: 宗翰襲遼帝于五院司，希尹為前驅，所將才八騎，與遼主戰，一日三敗之。

translations.literal: Zong Han attacked the Liao emperor at the Five Divisions office; Xi Yin was vanguard, leading only eight horsemen; fighting the Liao ruler, in one day he defeated him three times.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Han struck the Liao emperor at the Five Divisions office, Xi Yin rode ahead with only eight companions and, clashing with the Liao ruler, routed him three times in a single day.

sentences.zh: 明日，希尹得降人麻哲，言遼主在漠，委輜重，獎奔西京。

translations.literal: The next day Xi Yin obtained the surrenderer Mazhe, who said the Liao ruler was in the wilds, had abandoned baggage, and had fled at a rush toward the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Next day a defector named Mazhe told him the Liao emperor was in the open country, had cast off his train, and was racing for the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 幾及遼主于白水濼南。

translations.literal: He nearly caught the Liao ruler south of Baishui Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: He nearly overtook the Liao emperor south of Baishui Marsh.

sentences.zh: 遼主以輕騎遁去。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler escaped on light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor slipped away on a light escort.

sentences.zh: 盡獲其內庫寶物，遂至西京。

translations.literal: They seized all the inner-treasury treasures and then reached the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: They took the entire inner treasury and marched on to the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 西京降，使蒲察守之。

translations.literal: The Western Capital surrendered; he had Pucha garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Western Capital submitted, he left Pucha to hold it.

sentences.zh: 希尹至乙室部，不及遼主而還。

translations.literal: Xi Yin reached the Yishi tribe but, failing to overtake the Liao ruler, returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yin pushed into the Yishi lands, but unable to catch the Liao emperor, turned back.

sentences.zh: 及宗翰入朝，希尹權西南、西北兩路都統。

translations.literal: When Zong Han entered court, Xi Yin acted as commander-in-chief of the Southwest and Northwest circuits.
translations.idiomatic: While Zong Han was at court, Xi Yin served as acting commander-in-chief of the southwest and northwest circuits.

sentences.zh: 是時，夏人已受盟，遼主已獲，耶律大石自立，而夏國與婁室書責諸帥棄盟，軍入其境，多掠取者。

translations.literal: At this time the Western Xia had accepted the alliance and the Liao ruler had been taken; Yelü Dashi had declared himself ruler, yet Xia sent Wushu a letter rebuking the commanders for abandoning the pact—troops entering their territory with much plunder.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Western Xia had sworn alliance and the Liao emperor was captive; Yelü Dashi had set himself up as ruler, yet Xia wrote Wushu to reproach the Jin commanders for breaking faith—Jin columns were crossing the border and seizing goods at will.

sentences.zh: 希尹上其書，且奏曰：「聞夏使人約大石取山西諸郡，以臣觀之，夏盟不可信也。」

translations.literal: Xi Yin presented the letter and memorialized: "I hear Xia envoys have arranged with Dashi to take the Shanxi commanderies—in my view the Xia alliance cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yin forwarded the letter and memorialized: "I hear Xia envoys have agreed with Dashi to recover the Shanxi prefectures; in my judgment the Xia pact is not to be trusted."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「夏事酌宜行之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Handle Xia affairs as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Deal with Xia as circumstances require.

sentences.zh: 軍入其境，不知信與否也。

translations.literal: When troops enter their territory, one cannot know whether they are trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Once our armies cross their border, who can say whether they will keep faith?

sentences.zh: 大石合謀，不可不察，其嚴備之。」

translations.literal: Dashi's plotting cannot go unexamined—strictly guard against it."
translations.idiomatic: Dashi's designs must be watched; make your defenses strict."

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐宋，希尹為元帥右監軍。

translations.literal: When the great campaign against Song was launched, Xi Yin was right army supervisory commissioner under the commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the great expedition against Song, Xi Yin served as right supervisory commissioner on the commander's staff.

sentences.zh: 再伐宋，執二主以歸。

translations.literal: On the second campaign against Song, they brought back the two emperors captive.
translations.idiomatic: On the second invasion of Song they returned with both Song emperors as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 師還，賜希尹鐵券，除常赦不原之罪，餘釋不問。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Xi Yin was granted an iron certificate exempting him from crimes not normally pardoned; the rest were released without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he received an iron certificate pardoning all offenses save those never remitted by amnesty; lesser faults were passed over.

sentences.zh: 宗翰伐康王，希尹追之于揚州，康王遁去。

translations.literal: When Zong Han attacked Prince Kang, Xi Yin pursued him at Yangzhou; Prince Kang slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Han moved against Prince Kang, Xi Yin chased him to Yangzhou, but the prince escaped.

sentences.zh: 後與宗翰俱朝京師，請立熙宗為儲嗣，太宗遂以熙宗為諳班勃極烈。

translations.literal: Later, together with Zong Han he came to court at the capital and asked that Xizong be made heir; Taizong thereupon made Xizong an-ban bojilie.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Zong Han both attended court and urged that Xizong be named heir; Taizong then made Xizong an-ban bojilie.

sentences.zh: 皇統三年，上知希尹實無他心，而死非其罪，贈希尹儀同三司、邢國公，改葬之，蕭慶銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangtong the emperor knew Xi Yin truly had no other intent and that his death was not his crime; he posthumously granted Xi Yin Master of Palace Attendants and Duke of Xing, reburied him, and made Xiao Qing Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Blue Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangtong (1143) the throne acknowledged that Xi Yin had harbored no disloyalty and had died unjustly; he was posthumously made Master of Palace Attendants and Duke of Xing and given a new burial, and Xiao Qing was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Blue Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 天德三年，追封豫王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiande he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiande (1151) he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Yu.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，例降金源郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong, by precedent his rank was reduced to Prince of Jinyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong (1157), under the general demotion of princes, he was reduced to Prince of Jinyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 大定十五年，諡貞憲。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Dading he was given the posthumous title Zhenxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Dading (1175) his posthumous title was Zhenxian.

sentences.zh: 孫守道、守貞、守能。

translations.literal: Grandsons Shoudao, Shouzhen, and Shou Neng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons were Shoudao, Shouzhen, and Shou Neng.

sentences.zh: 守道自有傳。

translations.literal: Shoudao has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shoudao has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 孫 守貞

translations.literal: Grandson Shouzhen
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Shouzhen

sentences.zh: 守貞本名左靨，貞元二年，襲祖穀神謀克。

translations.literal: Shouzhen's original name was Zuoye; in the second year of Zhenyuan he inherited his grandfather's Gushen meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen, whose original name was Zuoye, in the second year of Zhenyuan (1195) inherited his grandfather's Gushen meng'an.

sentences.zh: 大定改元，收充符寶祗候，授通進，除彰德軍節度副使，遷北京留守，移上京。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title in Dading he was enrolled as insignia keeper, made Tongjin, appointed vice military governor of Zhangde Army, transferred to defender of the Northern Capital, then moved to the Supreme Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Dading gave way to a new reign, he entered the insignia service, became a Tongjin officer, was made vice military governor of Zhangde, then defender of the Northern Capital, and finally was posted to the Supreme Capital.

sentences.zh: 坐安置契丹戶民部內娶妻，杖一百，除名。

translations.literal: He was punished for taking a wife within the Khitan household resettlement bureau—one hundred blows and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted of marrying within the bureau that resettled Khitan households, flogged a hundred strokes, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，起為西京警巡使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was reappointed chief patrol officer of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year (1185) he was recalled as chief patrol officer of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗愛其剛直，授中都左警巡使，遷大興府治中，進同知，改同知西京留守事。

translations.literal: Shizong prized his forthrightness, made him left chief patrol officer of the Central Capital, moved him to executive of Daxing prefecture, advanced him to co-director, then made him co-director of Western Capital defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong admired his blunt integrity and appointed him left chief patrol officer of the Central Capital, then executive of Daxing prefecture, co-director, and finally co-director of the Western Capital administration.

sentences.zh: 禦史台奏守貞治有善狀，世宗因謂侍臣曰：「守貞勳臣子，又有材能，全勝其兄守道，它日可用也。」

translations.literal: The Censorate memorialized that Shouzhen's administration showed merit; Shizong therefore told attendants: "Shouzhen is the son of a meritorious minister and has talent—altogether surpasses his elder brother Shoudao; one day he may be put to use."
translations.idiomatic: When the Censorate reported his good record, Shizong told his attendants, "Shouzhen is a minister's son with real ability—better in every way than his brother Shoudao; we shall have use for him yet."

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，召為刑部尚書，兼右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong took the throne, Shouzhen was summoned as Minister of Punishments and concurrently Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhangzong's accession he was called up as Minister of Punishments and concurrent Right Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 守貞與修起居注張暐奏言：「唐中書門下入閤，諫官隨之，欲其預聞政事，有所開說。

translations.literal: Shouzhen and Veritable Records editor Zhang Wei memorialized: "In Tang, when the Secretariat entered the inner court, remonstrators followed, wishing to hear affairs beforehand and offer counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen and Zhang Wei, editor of the Veritable Records, submitted: "Under the Tang, when the Secretariat entered the inner court, remonstrators went with them so they might hear policy in advance and speak up.

sentences.zh: 又起居郎、起居舍人，每皇帝視朝，左右對立，有命則臨階俯聽，退而書之，以為起居注。

translations.literal: Again, the attendance masters and attendance clerks, whenever the emperor held court, stood left and right; when there was a command they leaned from the steps to listen, and on retiring wrote it down as the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: The attendance masters and clerks likewise stood to either side at every audience; when the emperor spoke they listened from the steps and afterward set it down in the record.

sentences.zh: 緣侍從官每遇視朝，正合侍立。

translations.literal: Because attendant officials on each audience ought rightly to stand in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants at court are meant to stand by during audiences.

sentences.zh: 自來左司上殿，諫官、修起居注不避，或侍從官除授及議便遣，始令避之。

translations.literal: Formerly when the Left Office went up to the hall, remonstrators and Veritable Records editors did not withdraw; only when attendant officials were appointed or dismissed, or when convenient missions were discussed, were they told to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when the Left Office attended the throne, remonstrators and record-keepers did not withdraw; withdrawal was ordered only for appointments among attendants or for discussion of special commissions.

sentences.zh: 比來一例令臣等回避，及香閤奏陳言文字，亦不令臣等侍立。

translations.literal: Recently we have been made to withdraw in every case alike, and when memorials are read in the incense pavilion we are not allowed to stand by either.
translations.idiomatic: Lately we are sent away without distinction, and when documents are read in the incense pavilion we are not permitted to remain.

sentences.zh: 則凡有聖訓及所議政事，臣等無緣得知，何所記錄，何所開說，似非本設官之義。

translations.literal: Then whenever there are imperial instructions or policies debated, we have no way to learn of them—what is there to record, what to remonstrate about?—which seems contrary to the purpose for which these offices were established.
translations.idiomatic: If we cannot hear the emperor's words or the business debated, what can we record or remonstrate upon? That defeats the reason these posts exist.

sentences.zh: 若漏泄政事，自有不密罪。」

translations.literal: If affairs leak, there is the crime of indiscretion in any case."
translations.idiomatic: Leaks of state business carry their own penalty for breach of secrecy."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋為賀宋生日使，還拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was envoy to congratulate the Song emperor's birthday; on return he was made Participant in Government.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to congratulate the Song emperor's birthday, and on his return was made Participant in Government.

sentences.zh: 時上新即政，頗銳意於治，嘗問漢宣帝綜核名實之道，其施行之實果何如。

translations.literal: The new emperor was keen on governance and once asked how Han Xuandi's method of weighing names against facts actually worked in practice.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor was eager to govern and once asked how Emperor Xuandi of Han had matched names to deeds in practice.

sentences.zh: 守貞誦「樞機周密，品式詳備」以對，上曰：「行之果何始？」

translations.literal: Shouzhen quoted "machinery close-woven, standards detailed and complete" in reply; the emperor said: "Where does one actually begin to carry it out?"
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen answered with the phrase "machinery close-woven, standards detailed and complete"; the emperor said, "But where does execution truly begin?"

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「在陛下厲精無倦耳。」

translations.literal: Shouzhen said: "It lies in Your Majesty's tireless diligence."
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen said, "In Your Majesty's unwearying effort alone."

sentences.zh: 久之，進尚書左丞，授上京世襲謀克。

translations.literal: After long service he was advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and granted the hereditary meng'an at the Supreme Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and given the hereditary meng'an at the Supreme Capital.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年夏，旱，天子下詔罪己。

translations.literal: In the third summer of Mingchang there was drought; the Son of Heaven issued an edict blaming himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year of Mingchang (1192) drought struck, and the emperor published a self-reproach.

sentences.zh: 守貞惶恐，表乞解職。

translations.literal: Shouzhen in fear memorialized begging to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen, shaken, asked to be relieved of office.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「天牆時雨，薦歲為災，所以警懼不逮。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Heaven withholds timely rain; years in succession bring disaster—this is to warn that our reach falls short.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Heaven withholds seasonable rain and harvests fail year after year, to warn Us that Our rule still falls short.

sentences.zh: 方與二三輔弼圖回遺闕，宜思有以助朕修政。

translations.literal: We are now with two or three chief counselors plotting to repair oversights—you should think how to help Us refine government.
translations.idiomatic: We are consulting chief ministers to mend what is lacking; you should find ways to help Us improve governance.

sentences.zh: 上答天戒，消沴召和，以康百姓。

translations.literal: Answer heaven's warning, dispel calamity and summon harmony, so that the people may prosper.
translations.idiomatic: Answer heaven's warning, dispel disaster, restore harmony, and bring ease to the people.

sentences.zh: 卿達機務，朕所親倚，而引咎求去，其如思助何。」

translations.literal: You grasp state affairs on which We lean closely, yet by taking blame you ask to leave—how does that aid Our wish for help?"
translations.idiomatic: You understand the machinery of state on which We rely, yet you take blame upon yourself and ask to go—how does that help Us seek remedy?"

sentences.zh: 守貞懇辭，乃出知東平府事。

translations.literal: Shouzhen earnestly declined; he was then sent out to govern Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouzhen pressed his resignation, he was sent out to administer Dongping.

sentences.zh: 命參知政事夾穀衡諭之曰：「卿勳臣之裔，早登潆無仕，才用聲績，朕所素知。

translations.literal: He ordered Participant in Government Jiagu Heng to instruct him: "You are the descendant of a meritorious minister and entered service early; your talent and reputation We have long known.
translations.idiomatic: The court charged Jiagu Heng to tell him: "You are born of a house that served the founding, you rose early in office, and your ability and standing are well known to Us.

sentences.zh: 故嗣位之初，擢任政府，於今數載，毗贊實多。

translations.literal: Therefore at the beginning of Our succession We raised you to the council; for several years now your support has been real.
translations.idiomatic: At Our accession We placed you in the central government, and for years your counsel has been of real weight.

sentences.zh: 既久任繁劇，宜均適逸安，矧內外之職，亦當更治，今特授卿是命。

translations.literal: Having long borne heavy duties, you should now share ease and rest; moreover inner and outer posts ought in turn to be refreshed—now We specially grant you this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Long service at the center has been taxing; it is right that you find ease, and that inner and outer offices alike see change—hence this new commission.

sentences.zh: 東平素號雄籓，兼比年饑歉，正賴經畫，卿其為朕往綏撫之。」

translations.literal: Dongping has always been called a great frontier; with famine these last years it depends on firm management—go pacify it for Us."
translations.idiomatic: Dongping is a great strategic prefecture, and famine has worn it thin—go there and settle it on Our behalf."

sentences.zh: 仍賜金幣、廄馬，以寵其行。

translations.literal: They also granted gold coins and stable horses to honor his departure.
translations.idiomatic: He was further given gold, silks, and horses from the imperial stables to mark his going.

sentences.zh: 它日，上問宰臣：「守貞治東平如何？」

translations.literal: Another day the emperor asked the chief ministers: "How does Shouzhen govern Dongping?"
translations.idiomatic: On another day the emperor asked his chief ministers, "How is Shouzhen doing at Dongping?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「亦不勞力。」

translations.literal: They replied: "He does not overexert himself."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "He does not strain himself."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「以彼之才，治一路誠有餘矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "With his talent, governing one circuit truly leaves him more than enough."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For a man of his gifts, one circuit is an easy charge."

sentences.zh: 右丞劉瑋曰：「方今人材無出守貞者，淹留於外，誠可惜也。」

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Liu Wei said: "Among men today none surpasses Shouzhen; to keep him long outside is a real pity."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei, the right vice director, added, "There is no talent today above Shouzhen's; it is a pity to leave him in the provinces."

sentences.zh: 上默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 尋改西京留守。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to defender of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made defender of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 監察禦史蒲刺都劾奏守貞前宴賜北部有取受事，不報。

translations.literal: Supervising censor Puladu memorialized that when Shouzhen had feasted and rewarded the northern tribes he had accepted bribes—the court took no action.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising censor Puladu accused Shouzhen of taking gifts when he feasted and rewarded the northern tribes; the memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 右拾遺路鐸上章辯之。

translations.literal: Right Reminder Lu Duo submitted a memorial in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duo, Right Reminder, memorialized in his defense.

sentences.zh: 四年，召拜平章政事，封蕭國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was summoned and made Grand Councilor, enfeoffed Duke of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1193) he was recalled as Grand Councilor and enfeoffed Duke of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 上禦後閤，召守貞曰：「朕以卿乃太師所舉，故特加委用。

translations.literal: The emperor received him in the rear hall and said: "We specially entrusted you because the Grand Preceptor recommended you.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving him in the rear hall, the emperor said, "I gave you unusual trust because the Grand Preceptor commended you.

sentences.zh: 然比者行事多太過，門下人少慎擇，複與丞相不協，以是令卿補外。

translations.literal: Yet lately your conduct has often gone too far, your staff have been chosen without care, and you again fell out with the chief councilor—for that We sent you to the provinces.
translations.idiomatic: But of late you have overreached, chosen your staff rashly, and quarreled with the chief councilor—that is why I sent you away.

sentences.zh: 載念我昭祖、太祖開創以來，乃祖佐命，積有勳勞，茲故召用。

translations.literal: Still, remembering how since Zhaozu and Taizu opened the enterprise your forebears aided the founding and piled up merit, We therefore call you back.
translations.idiomatic: Yet remembering that since Zhaozu and Taizu raised the dynasty your ancestors helped establish it and earned great merit, We summon you again.

sentences.zh: 卿其勉盡乃心，與丞相議事宜相和諧，率循舊章，無輕改革。」

translations.literal: Strive with all your heart; when you deliberate with the chief councilor be harmonious, follow the old statutes, and do not lightly change them."
translations.idiomatic: Give your whole mind to service; work in harmony with the chief councilor, keep to established rules, and do not reform them lightly."

sentences.zh: 因賜玉帶，並以蒲刺都所彈事與之，曰：「朕度卿必不爾，故以示卿。」

translations.literal: He then granted a jade belt and also gave him Puladu's accusation, saying: "We judged that you surely would not do such a thing, and therefore show this to you."
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed a jade belt and handed him Puladu's memorial, saying, "I was sure you had not done this; I show it so you may see what was said."

sentences.zh: 舊制，監宗禦史凡八員，漢人四員皆進士，而女直四員則文資右職參注。

translations.literal: By old rule there were eight supervising censors; four Han posts were all jinshi, while four Jurchen posts were filled from civil-status right-office appointees.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system there were eight supervising censors: the four Han seats went to jinshi, while the four Jurchen seats were filled from civil appointees of right-office rank.

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「監察乃清要之職，流品自異，俱宜一體純用進士。」

translations.literal: Shouzhen said: "Supervision is a pure, exalted post; its stream and grade differ—both ought uniformly to use only jinshi."
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen argued: "The censorate is a pure, eminent office with its own grade; both branches should alike recruit only jinshi."

sentences.zh: 一日奏事次，上問司吏移轉事。

translations.literal: One day during a memorial audience the emperor asked about rotating clerks in the offices.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, during business at court, the emperor asked about rotating clerks in the ministries.

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「今吏權重而積弊深，移轉為便。」

translations.literal: Shouzhen said: "Today clerks are weighty in power and deep in accumulated abuses—rotation would be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen said, "Clerks now wield too much power and abuses are entrenched; rotation would help."

sentences.zh: 上嘗歎文士卒無如党懷英者，守貞奏進士中若趙渢、王庭筠甚有時譽。

translations.literal: The emperor once sighed that among civil officials none matched Dang Huaiying; Shouzhen memorialized that among jinshi, Zhao Feng and Wang Tingjian enjoyed great repute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once lamented that no civil official equaled Dang Huaiying; Shouzhen named Zhao Feng and Wang Tingjian among the jinshi as men of wide esteem.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「出倫者難得耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Men who stand above the common run are hard to obtain."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Truly outstanding men are hard to find."

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「間世之才，自古所難。

translations.literal: Shouzhen said: "Talent of an age apart has been hard to obtain since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen said, "Men of once-in-an-age talent have always been rare.

sentences.zh: 然國家培養久，則人材將自出矣。」

translations.literal: Yet if the state cultivates them long, talent will emerge of itself."
translations.idiomatic: But if the state nurtures men over time, talent will appear on its own."

sentences.zh: 守貞因言：「國家選舉之法，惟女直、漢人進士得人居多，此舉更宜增取。

translations.literal: Shouzhen went on: "In the state's selection system, Jurchen and Han jinshi yield the most able men—this examination should take more.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen added, "In our selection system, Jurchen and Han jinshi supply the best men; this examination should admit more.

sentences.zh: 其諸司局承應人舊無出身，大定後才許敘使。

translations.literal: Attendants in the various bureaus formerly had no formal rank; only after Dading were they allowed regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau attendants once had no formal pedigree; only after Dading could they receive regular appointments.

sentences.zh: 經童之科，古不常設，唐以諸道表薦，或取五人至十人。

translations.literal: The classic-youth examination was not regularly established in antiquity; Tang used provincial recommendations, sometimes taking five to ten.
translations.idiomatic: The juvenile classics examination was not a standing institution in antiquity; the Tang relied on provincial recommendations, taking anywhere from five to ten.

sentences.zh: 近代以為無補，罷之。

translations.literal: Recent times deemed it useless and abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages judged it useless and abolished it.

sentences.zh: 本朝皇統間，取及五十人，因為常選。

translations.literal: Under Huangtong in our dynasty as many as fifty were taken, and it became a regular selection.
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty under Huangtong, fifty were admitted and it became a regular examination.

sentences.zh: 天德間，尋以停罷。

translations.literal: In Tiande it was soon suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tiande it was soon discontinued.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，複立是科，朝廷寬大，放及百數，誠恐積久不勝銓擬。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty took the throne the examination was restored; the court was generous and admitted on the order of a hundred—I truly fear that over time selection cannot keep pace.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty acceded, the examination was restored; the court has been liberal and admitted on the order of a hundred—I fear that in time the personnel office cannot keep up.

sentences.zh: 宜稍裁減，以清流品。」

translations.literal: It should be trimmed somewhat to keep the grades pure."
translations.idiomatic: It should be cut back somewhat to preserve the purity of rank."

sentences.zh: 又言節用省費之道，並嘉納焉。

translations.literal: He also spoke on economizing and saving expense; all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke on thrift and saving expense; the emperor approved everything.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄭王允蹈等伏誅，上以其家產均給諸王，戶部郎中李敬義言恐因之生事，上又以董壽為宮籍監都管勾，並下尚書省議。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince of Zheng Yuntao and others were executed; the emperor divided their estates among the princes; Li Jingyi of the Revenue Section warned this might cause trouble; the emperor also made Dong Shou superintendent of the palace registry—all were referred to the Ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince of Zheng Yuntao and others were put to death; the emperor divided their estates among the princes; Li Jingyi of the Revenue Section warned that trouble might follow; the emperor also appointed Dong Shou superintendent of the palace registry—all were sent to the Ministry for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 守貞奏：「陛下欲以允蹈等家產分賜懿親，恩命已出，恐不可改。

translations.literal: Shouzhen memorialized: "Your Majesty wishes to divide Yuntao's estate among imperial kin; the grace decree has gone forth and likely cannot be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen submitted: "Your Majesty means to divide Yuntao's estate among the imperial kin; the gracious order has already been issued and likely cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 今已減諸王弓矢，府慰司其出入，臣以為賜之無害。

translations.literal: Bows and arrows of the princes have already been reduced and the princely residence office controls their comings and goings—I think gifting it does no harm.
translations.idiomatic: The princes' bows and arrows have already been reduced and the princely residence office oversees their movements—I believe the gift does no harm.

sentences.zh: 如董壽罪人也，特恩釋之，已為幸矣，不宜更加爵賞。」

translations.literal: As for Dong Shou, a guilty man—special grace freed him; that is fortune enough; he should not receive further rank or reward."
translations.idiomatic: Dong Shou is a convicted man; special grace already spared him—that is fortune enough—and he should not receive further rank or reward."

sentences.zh: 上是守貞所言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved Shouzhen's words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted Shouzhen's advice.

sentences.zh: 自明昌初，北邊屢有警，或請出兵擊之。

translations.literal: From the start of Mingchang there were repeated alarms on the northern border; some urged sending troops to strike.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning of Mingchang the northern frontier was repeatedly alarmed, and some urged sending troops to attack.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「今方南議塞河，而複用兵於北，可乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "We are just deliberating in the south on blocking the river—can we also use troops in the north?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "We are just debating the southern dike in the south—can we also commit forces in the north?

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「彼屢突軼吾圉，今一懲之，後當不復來，明年可以見矣。」

translations.literal: Shouzhen said: "They have repeatedly raided our borders; punish them once and they will not come again—we shall see next year."
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen said, "They have repeatedly raided our borders; punish them once and they should not return—we shall know next year."

sentences.zh: 上因論守禦之法。

translations.literal: The emperor then discussed methods of defense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then discussed frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 守貞曰：「惟有皇統以前故事，舍此無法耳。」

translations.literal: Shouzhen said: "Only the precedents before Huangtong—there is no other way."
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen said, "Only the precedents from before Huangtong—beyond that there is no method."

sentences.zh: 先是，上以疑忌誅鄭王允蹈，後張汝弼妻高陀斡獄起，意又若在鎬王允中。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had Prince of Zheng Yuntao executed on suspicion; later the case of Zhang Rubi's wife Gaotuo'er arose and his mind again seemed fixed on Prince of Hao Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor executed Prince of Zheng Yuntao on suspicion; later the case of Zhang Rubi's wife Gaotuo'er arose, and his suspicions again seemed to fall on Prince of Hao Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 時右諫議大夫賈守謙上疏陳時事，思有以寬解上意。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrator Jia Shouqian memorialized on current affairs, hoping to ease the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Right Remonstrator Jia Shouqian memorialized on current affairs, hoping to relieve the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 右拾遺路鐸繼之，言尤切直。

translations.literal: Right Compiler Lu Duo followed, his words especially blunt.
translations.idiomatic: Right Compiler Lu Duo followed with words especially blunt.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 守貞持其事，獄久不決。

translations.literal: Shouzhen held the case; the trial long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen held the case, and the trial dragged on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 帝疑有黨，乃出守貞知濟南府事，仍命即辭，前舉守貞者董師中、路鐸等皆補外，上語宰臣曰：「守貞固有才力，至其讀書，方之真儒則未也。

translations.literal: Suspecting a faction, the emperor sent Shouzhen to govern Jinan and ordered immediate departure; those who had praised him—Dong Shizhong, Lu Duo—were all posted outside; he told the chief ministers: "Shouzhen has real ability; as to his learning, compared with true Confucians he falls short.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting a clique, the emperor sent Shouzhen to administer Jinan and ordered him to leave at once; those who had recommended him—Dong Shizhong, Lu Duo, and others—were all sent to provincial posts; he told his chief ministers, "Shouzhen has real ability, but in learning he does not measure up to true Confucians.

sentences.zh: 然太邀權譽，以彼之才而能平心守正，朝廷豈可少離。

translations.literal: Yet he courts reputation too eagerly; with his talent, if he could keep an even mind and uphold integrity, the court could hardly spare him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he courts reputation too eagerly; with his talent, if he could keep an even mind and hold to what is right, the court could hardly do without him.

sentences.zh: 今茲令出，蓋思之熟矣。」

translations.literal: This order now issued—I have thought it through thoroughly."
translations.idiomatic: This order now issued—I have thought it through."

sentences.zh: 俄以在政府日嘗與近侍竊語宮掖事，而妄稱奏下，上命有司鞫問，守貞款伏，奪官一階，解職。

translations.literal: Soon, for having privately discussed palace affairs with close attendants while in government and falsely claiming he had memorialized, the emperor ordered inquiry; Shouzhen confessed fully, lost one rank, and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, because while in government he had privately discussed palace affairs with close attendants and falsely claimed he had memorialized, the emperor ordered an inquiry; Shouzhen confessed fully, was stripped of one rank, and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 遣中使持詔責諭之曰：「挾奸罔上，古有常刑，結援養交，臣之大戒。

translations.literal: An imperial envoy bore an edict reproaching him: "Harbouring treachery and deceiving the sovereign—antiquity had fixed punishments; courting faction and cultivating connections—the great taboo of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial envoy bore an edict of reproof: "To harbour treachery and deceive the sovereign—antiquity had fixed punishments for that; to court allies and cultivate connections is the great taboo of ministers.

sentences.zh: 孰謂予相，乃蹈厥辜。

translations.literal: Who would say Our minister could tread such guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought Our minister would commit such crimes?

sentences.zh: 爾本出勳門，浸登膴仕。

translations.literal: You sprang from a meritorious house and gradually reached comfortable office.
translations.idiomatic: You came from a house of merit and gradually rose to comfortable office.

sentences.zh: 朕初嗣位，亟欲用卿。

translations.literal: When We first succeeded to the throne We urgently wished to employ you.
translations.idiomatic: When We first succeeded to the throne, We urgently wished to use you.

sentences.zh: 未閱歲時，升為宰輔，每期納誨，共致太平。

translations.literal: Within a year you rose to chief councilor; We looked for your counsel to bring peace together.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year had passed you rose to chief councilor; We expected your remonstrance and hoped to achieve peace together.

sentences.zh: 蓋求所長，不考其素，拔擢不為不峻，任用不為不專。

translations.literal: Seeking your strengths without examining your character—promotion was not shallow, trust was not stinted.
translations.idiomatic: We sought your strengths without examining your character; your promotion was not shallow, nor Our trust stinted.

sentences.zh: 曾報效之綽思，輒私權之自樹，交通近侍，密問起居，窺測上心，預圖趨向。

translations.literal: Your generous mind once pledged service, yet you promptly built private power, dealt with close attendants, secretly inquired after Our wellbeing, probed Our heart, and plotted ahead for favour.
translations.idiomatic: You once pledged broad service, yet you promptly built private power, trafficked with close attendants, secretly inquired after Our wellbeing, probed Our mind, and schemed ahead for favour.

sentences.zh: 繇患失之心重，故欺君之罪彰，指所無之事而妄以肆誣，實未始有言而謂之嘗諫。

translations.literal: From heavy fear of losing office, your crime of deceiving the sovereign shone forth—you pointed at things that never were and recklessly slandered; there had in truth been no words, yet you claimed you had remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Because fear of losing office weighed so heavily, your crime of deceiving the sovereign stood clear: you pointed at things that never were and recklessly slandered; there had in truth been no remonstrance, yet you claimed you had spoken.

sentences.zh: 義豈知於歸美，意專在於要君。

translations.literal: How could righteousness know returning praise? Your intent lay solely in coercing the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: How could righteousness know returning praise to the throne? Your intent lay solely in coercing the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 其飾詐之若然，豈為臣之當耳。

translations.literal: To dress fraud as truth—is that what a minister should do?
translations.idiomatic: To dress fraud as truth—is that what a minister should do?

sentences.zh: 複觀彈奏，益見私情，求親識之援而列布宮中，縱罪廢之余而出入門下。

translations.literal: Reviewing further accusations, private intent showed clearer—seeking allies among acquaintances you planted them in the palace and let men stripped and ruined pass through your gate.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing further accusations, your private designs showed clearer still: you sought allies among acquaintances and placed them in the palace, and let men stripped of office and ruined pass through your gate.

sentences.zh: 而又凡有官使，斂為己恩，謂皆涉於回邪，不宜任之中外。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever there was an imperial envoy you gathered the favour to yourself, alleging all were tainted with evil and unfit for office within or without.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, whenever there was an imperial envoy you gathered the credit to yourself, alleging that all were tainted with evil and unfit for office at court or in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 質之清議，固所不容，揆之乃心，烏得無愧。

translations.literal: Put to honest opinion you could not be borne; weighed against your heart, how could you not be ashamed?
translations.idiomatic: Put to honest public opinion you could not be tolerated; weighed against your own heart, how could you not be ashamed?

sentences.zh: 姑從輕典，庸示蒲懲。」

translations.literal: For now We apply the lighter statute, merely to show a token punishment."
translations.idiomatic: For now We apply the lighter statute, merely to show a token punishment."

sentences.zh: 仍以守貞不公事，宣諭百官於尚書省。

translations.literal: The affair of Shouzhen's unfair conduct was also announced to all officials at the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The matter of Shouzhen's misconduct was also proclaimed to all officials at the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 承安元年，降授河中防禦使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Cheng'an he was demoted to Defender of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Cheng'an (1196) he was demoted to Defender of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 五年，改部羅火紮石合節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Military Governor of the Buluohuo Zha'shihe alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1200) he was made military governor of the Buluohuo Zha'shihe alliance.

sentences.zh: 過闕，上賜手詔責諭之，令赴職。

translations.literal: Passing the capital, the emperor gave a handwritten edict of reproof and ordered him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When he passed the capital, the emperor bestowed a handwritten edict of reproof and ordered him to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷知都府事。

translations.literal: After long service he was transferred to administer the supreme capital.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was transferred to administer the Supreme Capital.

sentences.zh: 時南鄙用兵，上以山東重地，須大臣安撫，乃移知濟南府，卒。

translations.literal: When war raged on the southern frontier, Shandong being vital, a great minister was needed to pacify it—he was moved to Jinan and died there.
translations.idiomatic: War was then raging on the southern frontier; Shandong being a vital region, a great minister was needed to pacify it—he was transferred to administer Jinan and died there.

sentences.zh: 上聞而悼之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he mourned him.

sentences.zh: 敕有司致祭，賻贈禮物依故平章政事蒲察通例。

translations.literal: He ordered the offices to perform rites and gifts of condolence by the precedent of the late Chief Councilor Pucha Tong.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the offices to perform funeral rites and condolence gifts by the precedent of the late Chief Councilor Pucha Tong.

sentences.zh: 諡曰肅。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Su.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Su.

sentences.zh: 守貞剛直明亮，凡朝廷論議及上有所問，皆傳經以對。

translations.literal: Shouzhen was upright and clear; in all court debate and imperial questions he answered by citing the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen was upright and forthright; in all court deliberation and whenever the emperor questioned him, he answered by citing the classics.

sentences.zh: 上嘗與泛論人材，守貞乃跡其心術行事，臧否無少隱，故為胥持國輩所忌，竟以直罷。

translations.literal: Once when the emperor broadly discussed talent, Shouzhen traced men's motives and deeds, praising or blaming without concealment—hence Xu Chiguo and his sort resented him and he was dismissed for bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the emperor broadly discussed talent, Shouzhen traced men's motives and conduct, praising or blaming without concealment; Xu Chiguo and his like resented him, and he was dismissed in the end for his bluntness.

sentences.zh: 後趙秉文由外官入翰林，遽上書言：「願陛下進君子退小人。」

translations.literal: Later Zhao Bingwen entered the Hanlin from outside office and at once memorialized: "May Your Majesty advance gentlemen and dismiss petty men."
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhao Bingwen entered the Hanlin from a provincial post and at once memorialized: "May Your Majesty advance gentlemen and dismiss petty men."

sentences.zh: 上問君子小人謂誰。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked whom he meant by gentlemen and petty men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked whom he meant by gentlemen and petty men.

sentences.zh: 秉文對：「君子故相完顏守貞，小人今參知政事胥持國。」

translations.literal: Bingwen answered: "The gentleman is former Chief Councilor Wanyan Shouzhen; the petty man is today's Vice Councilor Xu Chiguo."
translations.idiomatic: Bingwen answered, "The gentleman is former Chief Councilor Wanyan Shouzhen; the petty man is today's Vice Councilor Xu Chiguo."

sentences.zh: 其為天下推重如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he esteemed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus was he esteemed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 孫 守能

translations.literal: Grandson: Shou Neng
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Shou Neng

sentences.zh: 守能本名胡刺，累官商州刺史。

translations.literal: Shou Neng, original name Huci, rose through offices to Governor of Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Neng, whose original name was Huci, rose through offices to governor of Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，宋人陷商州，守能被執。

translations.literal: Near the end of Zhenglong the Song took Shangzhou and Shou Neng was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Zhenglong the Song captured Shangzhou and Shou Neng was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 大定五年，宋人請和，誓書曰：「俘虜之人，盡數發還。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dading the Song sued for peace; the oath read: "Captives shall all be returned in full."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dading (1165) the Song sued for peace; the oath read, "All captives shall be returned in full."

sentences.zh: 完顏仲為報問國信使，求守能及新息縣令完顏按辰于宋，遂與俱歸。

translations.literal: Wanyan Zhong as returning envoy sought Shou Neng and Xinxi magistrate Wanyan An'chen from the Song; they returned together.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Zhong, as returning envoy, requested Shou Neng and Xinxi magistrate Wanyan An'chen from the Song, and they returned together.

sentences.zh: 守能等至京師，入見，詔給舊官之俸。

translations.literal: Shou Neng and the others reached the capital, were received in audience, and ordered given their former salaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou Neng and the others reached the capital and were received in audience, an edict restored their former salaries.

sentences.zh: 大定十九年，為西北路招討使。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Dading he became Commissioner to Pacify the Northwest Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Dading (1179) he became commissioner to pacify the Northwest Circuit.

sentences.zh: 是時，詔徙窩斡餘黨於臨潢、泰州。

translations.literal: At that time an order moved the remnants of Waqra's faction to Linhuang and Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict moved the remnants of Waqra's faction to Linhuang and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 押刺民列嘗從窩斡，其弟閘敵也當徙，偽稱身亡，以馬賂守能，固匿不遣。

translations.literal: Yamin of the Bila tribe had followed Waqra; his brother Zhadie'ye was due for resettlement but falsely claimed death, bribed Shou Neng with horses, and was hidden and not sent.
translations.idiomatic: Yamin of the Bila tribe had once followed Waqra; his brother Zhadie'ye was due for resettlement but falsely claimed to have died, bribed Shou Neng with horses, and was deliberately hidden and not sent away.

sentences.zh: 及受賕補賽也蕃部通事，事覺。

translations.literal: He also took bribes to appoint Saiye as tribal interpreter—the matter came to light.
translations.idiomatic: He also took bribes to appoint Saiye as tribal interpreter for the Fan department—the matter came to light.

sentences.zh: 是時，烏古里石壘部族節度副使奚沙阿補杖殺無罪鎮邊猛安，尚書省俱奏其事。

translations.literal: At the same time Xi Sha'abu, vice military governor of the Wuguli Shilei tribes, beat to death an innocent frontier meng'an; the Ministry memorialized both cases together.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Xi Sha'abu, vice military governor of the Wuguli Shilei tribal command, flogged to death an innocent frontier meng'an; the Ministry memorialized both cases together.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「守能由刺史超擢至此，敢恣貪墨。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Shou Neng was leapt from governor to this post yet dares to indulge in corruption.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Shou Neng was promoted in one leap from governor to this post, yet he dares to indulge in corruption.

sentences.zh: 向者招討司官多進良馬、橐駝、鷹鶻等物，蓋假此以率斂爾，自今並罷之。」

translations.literal: Formerly pacification commissioners often presented fine horses, camels, hawks, and falcons—surely using these to extort; from now all that is ended."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly pacification commissioners often presented fine horses, camels, hawks, and falcons—surely using these to extort; from now on all of that is abolished."

sentences.zh: 因責其兄守道曰：「守能自刺史躐遷招討，外官之尊，無以逾此。

translations.literal: He then reproached his brother Shoudao: "Shou Neng vaulted from governor to pacification commissioner—the honour among outside posts cannot exceed this.
translations.idiomatic: He then reproached his brother Shoudao: "Shou Neng vaulted from governor to pacification commissioner—the honour among provincial posts cannot exceed this.

sentences.zh: 前招討哲典以貪墨伏誅，守能豈不知，乃敢如此，其意安在。

translations.literal: The former commissioner Zhedian was executed for corruption—how could Shou Neng not know? Yet he dares this—what is his intent?
translations.idiomatic: The former commissioner Zhedian was executed for corruption—how could Shou Neng not know? Yet he dares this—what is his intent?

sentences.zh: 爾之親弟，何不先訓戒之也。」

translations.literal: Your own younger brother—why did you not warn him beforehand?"
translations.idiomatic: He is your own younger brother—why did you not warn him beforehand?"

sentences.zh: 上謂宰臣曰：「監察專任糾彈。

translations.literal: He told the chief ministers: "Supervising censors exist solely to impeach.
translations.idiomatic: He told his chief ministers, "Supervising censors exist solely to impeach.

sentences.zh: 宗州節度使阿思懣初之官，途中侵擾百姓，到官舉動皆違法度。

translations.literal: When Ashen first took office as military governor of Zongzhou, he harassed the people on the road; once in office every act violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: When Ashen first took office as military governor of Zongzhou, he harassed the people along the way; once in office every act violated the law.

sentences.zh: 完顏守能為招討使，貪冒狼籍。

translations.literal: Wanyan Shou Neng as pacification commissioner was greedy and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Shou Neng as pacification commissioner was greedy and lawless.

sentences.zh: 凡達官貴人，皆未嘗舉劾。

translations.literal: Yet for all high officials and nobles, none had ever been impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Yet for all high officials and nobles, none had ever been impeached.

sentences.zh: 斡睹只群牧副使僕散那也取部人球杖兩枝，即便彈奏。

translations.literal: Wuduzhi deputy herds master Pusan Naye took two ball-sticks from his tribesmen and was impeached at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wuduzhi deputy herds master Pusan Naye took two ball-sticks from his tribesmen and was impeached at once.

sentences.zh: 自今，監察禦史職事修舉，然後遷除。

translations.literal: From now on, supervising censors shall be promoted only after they have performed their duties properly.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, supervising censors shall be promoted only after they have properly performed their duties.

sentences.zh: 不舉職者，大則降罰，小則決責，仍不得去職。」

translations.literal: Those who fail in duty shall, in serious cases, be demoted and penalized, in minor cases flogged, and in neither case may they leave office."
translations.idiomatic: Those who fail in duty shall, in serious cases, be demoted and penalized, in minor cases flogged, and in neither case may they leave their posts."

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏，守能兩贓俱不至五十貫，抵罪。

translations.literal: The Ministry reported: Shou Neng's two bribes each fell short of fifty strings—liable under law.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry reported that Shou Neng's two bribes each fell short of fifty strings and that he was liable under law.

sentences.zh: 奚沙阿補解見居官，並解世襲謀克。

translations.literal: Xi Sha'abu was dismissed from his current post and stripped of hereditary meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Sha'abu was dismissed from his current post and stripped of hereditary meng'an.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此舊制之誤。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is an error in the old regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is an error in the old regulation.

sentences.zh: 居官犯除名者，與世襲並罷之，非犯除名者勿罷。」

translations.literal: Those dismissed from office for crimes meriting expulsion lose hereditary meng'an together; those not so expelled should not lose it."
translations.idiomatic: Those dismissed from office for crimes meriting expulsion shall lose hereditary meng'an together; those not expelled for such crimes should not lose it."

sentences.zh: 遂著於令。

translations.literal: This was then written into statute.
translations.idiomatic: This was then written into statute.

sentences.zh: 特詔守能杖二百，除名。

translations.literal: By special edict Shou Neng received two hundred blows and expulsion.
translations.idiomatic: By special edict Shou Neng was flogged two hundred strokes and expelled from office.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：阿離合懣之善頌，宗雄之強識，希尹之敏學，益之以征伐之功，豈不偉哉。

translations.literal: Appraisal: Ali Hemen's gift for praise, Zong Xiong's strong memory, Xi Yin's quick learning—add campaigns won, are they not grand?
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Ali Hemen's gift for praise, Zong Xiong's strong memory, Xi Yin's quick learning—with the merit of campaigns added, are they not grand?
